meta.title: Ainize — critical UX review 4: chained purchases and the peer-to-peer sharing economy

summary:
Ainize is a peer-to-peer marketplace for "knowledge": small trained memory-table patches (.npz) that anyone can load into a running LLM, live-test, publish and be paid for. There is no operator in the middle. Every node is a peer that sells its own knowledge, verifies other people's, and settles payments node-to-node — as node credit on a local record DAG, or as AIN transfers on the AI Network chain through an x402 gateway (402 → pay → X-PAYMENT → manifest → body). Knowledge carries lineage, so a sale pays the seller, the ancestors and the data providers by one rule; versions supersede; tracks bundle a daily bake; and two teach doors let a visitor turn their own questions into knowledge and be paid for it. Three earlier reviews covered the visitor's web (items 1–100), the terminal and the operator (101–169), and derivative publishing, composition and the daily bake (170–269). This one is about what the owner asked for: the cascade of purchases that a chained buy, a teach-on-top, a composition or a subscription sets off, and whether the sharing economy behind it holds up peer to peer.

**How it is supposed to work.** A peer shares rather than hoards because sharing pays better: publish a base, and every derivative anyone builds on it pays you a share of every sale, forever, without you doing anything. Buy a child and you see the whole family you are paying into — its parents, their prices, who receives what — and pay once, in one step, for the parts you do not already own. Teach on top of somebody's knowledge and the acquisition of that base is the first purchase in the chain; publish and the base's creator is credited on a record you both signed. Verify other people's work and the network pays you for the GPU minutes, because "Verified 2/2 by independent nodes" is the only thing a buyer's money rests on. Nothing needs a central party: the settle record on the shared ledger is the receipt, the anchor is the licence, the peers are the CDN.

**How the running product actually moves money and trust.** The primitives are real and several are excellent. A purchase is a millisecond-stamped timeline that checks the body's sha256 against the on-ledger anchor whichever peer served it; every settlement carries a full per-address royalty map that is broadcast to every node within a second, clamped so the payouts can never exceed the price; the AIN payout queue writes each row before it attempts the transfer and refuses to auto-retry one interrupted by a restart; the teacher's public earnings page distinguishes what is owed from what this node can see was paid, in careful words. Money really does cross nodes: buying a leaf on node-c credited node-b's wallet within seconds, and on the demo chain node-c has been sending 3 AIN per sale to node-a for two days. But the market around those primitives is not closed. **The paywall is "do you already have the file", and everyone who matters already has it**: every node is a verifier by default, a verifier downloads every announced body for free — the claim needs nothing but an unsigned POST — and `apply`, the live test and `subscribe` check only that the file is on disk. A body once held can be loaded, served, taught on and resubscribed forever without a settlement. On the AIN path the payment itself is a bearer ticket: the tx hash, not the payer, collects the file, and the real payer is told "payment already used". And a buyer who has the bytes can republish them, byte-identical, as their own root listing at a quarter of the price — whereupon the product marks the original SUPERSEDED and points every buyer at the copy. Meanwhile the honest paths leak in the other direction: a retry pays twice, a lost response loses the file with a recovery path nobody documents, a free item still runs the whole payment ceremony, and a node that changes its port loses every listing it ever published.

**The three biggest gaps.**

**1. Possession is the licence, so the people the economy depends on never pay.** `mayDownload` exempts any address that says it has the verifier role (market.ts:645-656) — the role every `ainize init` turns on and an unsigned `/p2p/hello` grants (api.ts:861-865); on the demo chain 91 of 132 registered nodes claim it. `applyPatch`, `testablePatches` and `subscribe` gate on `blobs.has` (market.ts:826-838, 1034-1038, 1108-1112), so a verified body is production-ready, free, forever, and the manifest's 24-hour token is a bearer anyone can pass on. Nothing refuses a byte-identical republish, and `reconcileSupersedes` will retire the original for the copier. The result is an economy in which the only participants who pay are those who do not run a node — and the participants who do run nodes are also the ones who could resell the file.

**2. The record says who is owed; nothing says who was paid.** The split is computed honestly and written to a public record — and then the money is a private matter between the seller and its own SQLite. `/api/me/wallet` builds "Creator revenue share received" from settle records (api.ts:345), so an ancestor reads 34 payments and 102 AIN while the seller's payout table has 29 rows and the chain's transfer path holds 8; nothing links a settlement to a payout tx, nothing rebuilds a lost payout row, an address spelled in two cases is paid once, a parent the seller's node cannot resolve is silently paid 0 %, and there is no way to move an earned balance anywhere at all. The product already contains the honest version of this screen — `teacherProfile`, which reports owed, paid, pending and "this node cannot see that transfer" — and the wallet does not use it.

**3. The work that makes the market trustworthy is unpaid, and the act that damages it is free.** In 501 attestations and 2,765 AIN of sales, verifiers have received nothing: there is no `verifierShare` anywhere in the code, no wallet row, no earnings screen, and no page that tells a new operator that the role costs a GPU, a gigabyte of other people's bodies and minutes of model lock per item. At the same time a challenge — the safeguard the terms offer in place of the deposit that was honestly removed — costs nothing, needs no reason, has no limit, and takes a rival off sale until somebody else spends GPU time; the network has recorded 0 FAILs and 0 challenges, and no screen says so. And the badge itself is thin: "2/2 independent verifiers" is satisfied by two processes sharing one model server, because an attestation records no executor, no duration and no sample count.

Underneath all three sits a smaller, fixable absence: nothing in the product ever prices a chain. There is no `requires[]` in the 402, no total before a family purchase, no quote before a subscription, no subscription price at all, no metering behind the "pay per hour loaded" and "pay per use" the forms offer, and no way to change a price after listing. The lineage work landed in L0/L1 gives the anchor the fields these fixes need — `derivation`, `base.stack`, `dataset`, a closed licence list — and no screen, gate or payout reads them yet.

Below: 100 problems worth fixing, numbered 270–369, grouped by flow and ranked within each; the table that follows lists the twenty that would change the economy most.

top20.title: A byte-identical copy of someone else's knowledge lists as a new root at a quarter of the price — and automatically retires the original
top20.fixed_note: Two halves, both closed. Draft time: createDraft refuses `duplicate_body` outright — with no --force override — when the exact bytes are already on the record under another author, and points at building on that knowledge instead. Record time: a supersede can only name an older anchor by the same author, so a copy can no longer retire the original (verified live with an overlapping rival publish from a second node). The original author is told: the node logs a warn event naming the copy, its author, its price and the shared sha the moment such an anchor arrives from a peer (verified live — a node that published the same bytes before it knew of the original was peered in, and the author's log carried the notice), and the manage page's overlap table now says who published each overlap and marks a byte-identical republish as one. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — publishing another node’s exact bytes is refused with duplicate_body, and --force does not override it.

top20.title: Anyone who says they are a verifier downloads every knowledge body for free — the claim is an unsigned POST, and 91 of 132 node records on the demo chain already make it
top20.fixed_note: POST /p2p/hello records an address and its roles only when the caller signs `hello:<endpoint>`, and the blanket verifier exemption became a verification lease — the entry must be waiting for that verifier, the lease ends when its attestation lands, at most three fetches, each logged on the seller. Verified live: a throwaway key claiming the role gets 402 instead of the body, and its claim is not recorded. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — an unsigned POST /p2p/hello claiming the verifier role is recorded as an endpoint with address null, and GET /p2p/blob/:sha answers 402.

top20.title: Possession is licence: apply, live-test, chat and subscribe check only that the file is on disk, so a verifier runs a seller's whole catalogue for free
top20.fixed_note: A `licenses` row records where the right to use a body came from, and a ’verification’ row is possession only — refused at apply, in the chat picker, in chat and in subscribe. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK found the fifth door still open: Teacher.contextTargets decided on blob presence alone, so on a verifier node `teach train --patch <someone-else’s>` loaded a verification copy, trained on top of it and would have published a lesson naming an unbought base. Reproduced live and closed in 6955ba1 (`knowledge_not_licensed`, GET /api/teach/bases/:id gains the matching reason, CLI + browser copy in EN+KO).

top20.title: An AIN payment is a bearer ticket: whoever presents the tx hash first collects the file, and the real payer is told 'payment already used'
top20.fixed_note: An AIN payment is bound to the quote it answers: the 402 carries `transfer_key = transferKeyFor(resource, nonce)`, AinLedger.transfer writes at that key instead of a random push id, and settlePayment requires tr.key to match, the nonce to be this node's and unused, and a `proof` over sha256("x402-ain:<tx>:<nonce>") signed by tr.from — so the manifest can only go to the address that paid. Verified live on the dev chain: a transfer with no quote key bought nothing; a watcher presenting the payer's tx hash was refused for want of a proof, and refused again when it signed with its own key; the payer redeemed, and redeemed again idempotently. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live against the AIN dev chain — packages/node/test/ain.test.ts now passes end to end, so a real transfer carrying the quote’s transfer_key and a proof over sha256("x402-ain:<tx>:<nonce>") is what redeems the manifest.

top20.title: Verifying is unpaid work: 501 attestations and 2,765 AIN of sales on the demo chain, and not one credit has ever reached a verifier
top20.fixed_note: The attestations that count for an entry are paid `verifier_share` (0.05 network floor) of the seller side of every sale: verified live on a throwaway cluster, where a 10-CREDIT sale settled {verifier 0.25, verifier 0.25, seller 9.5} and a lineage sale settled {parent author 3.175, verifier 0.175, seller 6.65}; the wallet, `ainize wallet` and the family-tree money card print what verifying earns. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live on the local cluster AND on the AIN dev chain — every settlement’s royalty map names the two verifiers at 0.1 of a 4 CREDIT sale beside the seller’s 3.8.

top20.title: One creator spelled two ways is paid once: 3 of 4.5 AIN never leaves the seller, and on a local ledger the rest lands on a string no wallet matches
top20.fixed_note: royaltyPlan sums addresses case-insensitively under their first-seen spelling, payouts.enqueue folds the spellings before inserting a row, and creditBalance and /api/me/wallet compare case-insensitively — one person in two spellings is now one payee with the summed amount. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: covered by the named core test and by creditBalance folding case on the live cluster.

top20.title: The ancestor's wallet reports the seller's promises as money received: 34 payments and 102 AIN on one screen, 29 payout rows on the seller's, 8 transfers on the chain
top20.fixed_note: Every wallet royalty row carries its own state — credited / paid / pending / failed / unconfirmed — asked of the seller's node through the new public GET /p2p/payouts/:hash, with owed / in-balance / transferred / unconfirmed totals on Account and in `ainize wallet`, so a promise can no longer be read as a receipt. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — GET /api/me/wallet separates owed/credited/paid/unconfirmed, names the state per row and reports verification income apart from lineage.

top20.title: A sale whose lineage does not resolve on the seller's node pays the seller 100 % and no record says why — 3 of 37 demo sales did exactly that
top20.fixed_note: An unresolved parent is paid through `parent_authors[i]`, or held back and written onto the settlement as `royalty_unresolved` with an error event on the seller — never folded into the seller's own line — and an over-distribution is scaled proportionally instead of paying the seller the whole price. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: covered by the named core test (an unresolved ancestor is paid through parent_authors or held back on the record).

top20.title: A purchase is not idempotent: a retry, a second click or a lost response pays the full price again — and the second payment overwrites the first purchase row
top20.fixed_note: ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: the earlier fixed:true (a5d2d3c) was optimistic and one of the two copies still read open. Reproduced live at HEAD — node-c bought adv-base, then `ainize patch buy adv-base` ran the whole 402 loop again and moved a second 4 CREDIT (96.425 -> 92.525) for a body already on disk. Market.buy now reads this node’s own receipt first (paidFor(): the ledger settlement, else the purchase row) and collects on it; `again: true` / `--again` / the web’s "pay a second time" control is the only way to pay twice. Verified live: the second buy leaves the balance untouched, --again still pays, POST /api/patches/:id/buy answers redeemed with total 0.

top20.title: The training set that makes a knowledge worth 25 AIN is a free download, and the promise that buys it — 'I am building on this' — is never checked
top20.fixed_note: A derive intent is now a recorded commitment: `derive_intents` stores which teaching key took which knowledge's questions and when, the response says what was promised, and the parent's owner can read the list. The promise is enforced — a lesson trained on a set that came from a published knowledge is refused at createJob and again at publish unless it names that knowledge as its base — and the publish sheet says what each access level means before the creator chooses. Node/web 473d2bc, CLI render 69c17fa.

top20.title: Buying a child buys the child alone: the quote is the child's price, and no surface says whether the base is needed, already inside, or what the family costs
top20.fixed_note: requires[]/total/self_contained on the 402, GET /api/patches/:id and /quote; buy({withRequired,maxTotal}); rendered on the Buy tab and printed by `patch buy`/`use`. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK found one residual, fixed in a2b3426: the 402’s `total` came from quoteFor, which subtracts what the ASKING node holds — and the asking node there is the seller, which owns its own bases, so a 5-CREDIT delta over a 4-CREDIT base quoted total 5 with self_contained false to every non-ainize x402 client. The 402 now carries the family LIST price (verified live: total 9); the buyer’s own /quote still subtracts its holdings.

top20.title: A challenge costs nothing, needs no reason, has no limit, and takes a rival off sale for as long as you keep filing them
top20.fixed_note: A challenge needs a 20-character reason, one address may hold only one open challenge per anchor and cannot re-file for 24 h after a re-run dismissed one, every challenge records upheld/dismissed on the entry, and the CLI prints what a challenge costs other operators before it sends. All three refusals reproduced live. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — a 3-character reason is refused (400), a second challenge while one is open is refused (409), and a real challenge is logged and answered.

top20.title: '2/2 independent verifiers' can be two processes on one host sharing one model server, and the record cannot tell the difference
top20.fixed_note: Every executed attestation carries an executor fingerprint (API origin, served model and the engine's own start time), deriveCatalog counts distinct engines and unknown ones separately, the knowledge page and `patch get` say how many model servers were behind the attestations, and a run on a node that already has the knowledge applied is refused rather than recorded as a verification. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: the counting half is reproduced live — `patch get` prints "2 attestations without an engine fingerprint" and the entry carries executors/executors_unknown. The fingerprint against a real engine stays deferred (no engine available).

top20.title: Subscribing spends the balance item by item, publishes the subscription before buying anything, and reports success when every purchase failed
top20.fixed_note: the node half: POST /api/branches/:name/quote prices every item before anything is spent, subscribe() buys everything BEFORE it appends and broadcasts the subscription record, a partial acquisition is 409 {acquired, failed[]} with nothing announced (verified live: the buyer keeps the three items it could afford, `mine: []`, and the gateway does not route to it), and the CLI asks [y/N] and exits non-zero. The web half shipped in 0d82cfb. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — `branch subscribe` prints the per-item plan and the total, asks before spending, refuses a non-terminal without --yes, and reports what was actually bought.

top20.title: On a local ledger every new keypair is worth 100 CREDIT: a seller's revenue is minted by whoever buys, and 'insufficient credit' is one key-rotation away
top20.fixed_note: Local credit is issued, not assumed: creditBalance sums a recorded `credit_grants` row plus royalties minus purchases, one grant per address written only after the buyer's signature proves the key exists, capped at market.creditGrants (default 100 addresses), never on a node that sells for AIN, and the node grants itself the same way at startup. GET /api/credit/:address says where the credit came from, how many grants are gone and that it is not money; the CLI quote and the Buy tab print that sentence where the money is about to be spent. Addresses are compared case-insensitively there too. Verified live: a fresh keypair's balance came from a recorded grant with a reason, and the issuance count moved 1 → 3. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — GET /api/credit/<never-seen address> answers balance 0 with would_grant, and a grant is recorded, capped and attributed once the address first signs a payment.

top20.title: A node that changes its port loses every listing it ever published: the gateway URL is frozen in the immutable anchor and nothing re-points it
top20.fixed_note: gatewaysFor() resolves the seller from the peer table and the node records, tries the candidates in order, and the frozen address on the record is the last of them. VERIFIED LIVE by moving a publisher from :3895 to :3896 after it announced: the buy went through the peer entry and the dead frozen URL was never reached. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK added the two surfaces that still printed the frozen address (requires[] in the 402 and the quote, and elsewhere[] in the chat picker) — c54a8e2.

top20.title: To teach on top of a knowledge this node does not hold there is no way to get it: the picker hides it, the CLI says 'unknown knowledge', and a visitor cannot buy at all
top20.fixed_note: GET /api/chat/patches now returns `elsewhere[]`: every knowledge this node's model could run but cannot load, with its price, its seller and the reason (not_held / verify_only), rendered as a disabled row in the picker with Buy for the operator and "ask this node to get it" for a visitor (POST /api/chat/patches/:id/request writes one demand event), and `ainize chat --list` prints the same table. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — a body held only because this node verified it appears under elsewhere[] with reason verify_only, not in items[].

top20.title: Nothing links a settlement to the payout that honoured it: the creator's share is an unreferenced transfer from the seller's wallet, after the fact
On a local-ledger node the teacher prices in play money and is later shown '4.9 CREDIT Paid' for credit a browser key can never spend
top20.fixed_note: The publish sheet renders `price.credit_note` under the price field and says where a payout actually lands on a local-ledger node; the teacher page carries the same note and relabels Paid as 'Credited on <node> (not withdrawable)'; `teach status` and `teach publish` print the ledger a price is denominated in. The node reports `ledger {kind, currency}` on the teach policy, the challenge and the teacher profile. Node/web 473d2bc, CLI 69c17fa. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — `teach publish` prints "settles in CREDIT on this node’s own ledger — development play money, not withdrawable", and the sheet renders price.credit_note.

top20.title: Any node can take over a track by re-creating it under the same name: subscribers follow the new owner and the original owner is locked out
top20.fixed_note: the node that first wrote a track name owns it: Market.branches() drops a `branch` record for that name from anyone else (and the local ledger applies the same rule the AIN write rule does), createBranch refuses with 409 branch_exists naming the owner — reproduced live — and the console track card shows the owner. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — node-b creating node-a’s track name is refused with branch_exists naming the owner.

flows.name: A. Chained purchases
flows.description: Buying into a family of knowledge — a child that depends on parents, a stack, an agent's budget — and everything the money touches on the way.

items.title: Buying a child buys the child alone: the quote is the child's price, and no surface says whether the base is needed, already inside, or what the family costs
items.surface: Knowledge page → Buy tab; `ainize use <child>`; `ainize patch buy`; `GET /x402/patch/:id`; `ainize-agent run --max-price`
items.problem: `requirementsFor` (packages/node/src/market.ts:655-666) quotes scheme, price, payTo, nonce and a description of the form `Knowledge patch <id> (<rows> rows, <model>)` — nothing about `anchor.parents`. `market.buy` (market.ts:757-820) never reads the parents either, and `applyPatch` (market.ts:826-838) loads the child by itself. The design's `requires: [{id, name, price, held}]` and its 'Buy both' sheet (docs/lineage-teach-design.md:111, 283-292) are not implemented anywhere, and the L1 anchor fields that would settle the question — `derivation.kind`, `base.export: 'delta'|'squash'` (packages/core/src/types.ts:146-176) — are on the record but on no screen and in no gate. So a buyer facing 'built on pixel-parent' cannot tell whether the file is complete on its own (today: always, because children are squashes) or whether they are about to need a second, unbudgeted purchase from another peer; the agent's `--max-price` (packages/agent/src/agent.ts:188) is a per-item budget for a purchase that may be a family.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-15-node-d-chain.txt (`use pixel-grandchild` → 2 CREDIT, grandchild applied alone, pixel-child and pixel-parent `purchased:false has_body:false`, and the model answers correctly from the grandchild alone); chain-buy-agent-08-private-leaf-buy-royalty.txt (402 fields for c-leaf; catalogue `parents:['p-mid']` with no price or gateway for it; the agent's `--max-price 60` passed on a 130-CREDIT family); chain-buy-human-08-child-operator-en-1280-buy.png (Buy tab: price, seller, gateway, nothing else). Re-read at HEAD: market.ts:655-666, 757-820, 826-838.
items.user_cost: Either money for a base the buyer already holds inside the child (5 CREDIT for 2,992 rows they just bought — see 283), or, once real delta patches ship, a paid file that does nothing until a second purchase from a peer whose price nobody quoted. The chain's real price is discovered one purchase at a time.
items.fix: In `requirementsFor` and `GET /api/patches/:id` return `requires: [{id, name, price, currency, gateway_url, author, held}]` computed from `anchor.parents` (walk to depth 16 like `royaltySplit`) plus `derivation.kind` and `base.export`, and render one sentence from them on the Buy tab (`packages/web/src/pages/PatchPage.tsx:494-506`): 'complete on its own — includes its base's 2,992 rows' or 'needs pixel-parent (5 CREDIT, node-a) — buy both'. `market.buy({withRequired:true})` buys ancestors deepest-first with one settle record each and returns `purchases[]` + `total`; `patchUse` prints the quote and asks (or `--yes`); the agent compares the TOTAL with `--max-price`.
items.fixed_note: requires[]/total/self_contained on the 402, GET /api/patches/:id and /quote; buy({withRequired,maxTotal}); rendered on the Buy tab and printed by `patch buy`/`use`. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK found one residual, fixed in a2b3426: the 402’s `total` came from quoteFor, which subtracts what the ASKING node holds — and the asking node there is the seller, which owns its own bases, so a 5-CREDIT delta over a 4-CREDIT base quoted total 5 with self_contained false to every non-ainize x402 client. The 402 now carries the family LIST price (verified live: total 9); the buyer’s own /quote still subtracts its holdings.

items.title: A purchase is not idempotent: a retry, a second click or a lost response pays the full price again — and the second payment overwrites the first purchase row
items.surface: `ainize patch buy <id>`; Buy tab 'Buy again'; `POST /api/patches/:id/buy`; `ainize-agent run`
items.problem: `market.buy` goes quorum → gateway → 402 → transfer with no lookup of an existing settlement or purchase row (market.ts:757-790); `store.putPurchase` (market.ts:812) is an INSERT OR REPLACE keyed by patch id, so the second payment erases the first one's tx hash. The web offers 'Buy again' as the only action on a purchased item (PatchPage.tsx:529) and the agent re-runs the whole 402 loop before checking `existsSync(dest)` (packages/agent/src/agent.ts:231). `mayDownload` already lets a settled buyer fetch the body for nothing (market.ts:651), so every one of these payments buys something the buyer was already entitled to.
items.evidence: critic-03-nodeb-rebuy-pixelplus.txt (node-b, already a buyer, `patch buy pixelplus-087600` → another 0.1 AIN moved, balance 1342.0 → 1341.9, purchases count still 1 — no local trace of two payments); chain-buy-agent-15-pay-again-for-held-body.txt (187 settle records from one agent identity for one 3.8 MB file = 18.7 AIN); chain-buy-human-19-demo-web-ain-buy-notes.json ('Buy again' → real transfer, 'body already present').
items.user_cost: Real money for nothing, repeatedly: a mis-click, a dropped connection, a cron'd agent or a cautious 'let me get it again' each costs the full price, and the buyer's own node cannot even show that it happened twice. At 25 AIN per item a nightly agent loop is a subscription nobody signed.
items.fix: Short-circuit in `market.buy`: if `store.getPurchase(id)` exists or `entry.settlements.some(s => s.buyer === this.address)`, fetch the manifest through the free signed path and record no new settle (return `{already:true}` from `POST /api/patches/:id/buy` unless `{force:true}`). Make `putPurchase` append rather than replace (a `purchases` history keyed by tx). In the web replace 'Buy again' with 'Download again (free)' / 'Load into model' (PatchPage.tsx:529) and keep a second licence behind an explicit confirm. In the agent, check `patches/<sha>.npz` and the purchases file (289) before touching the gateway.
items.fixed_note: ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: the earlier fixed:true (a5d2d3c) was optimistic and one of the two copies still read open. Reproduced live at HEAD — node-c bought adv-base, then `ainize patch buy adv-base` ran the whole 402 loop again and moved a second 4 CREDIT (96.425 -> 92.525) for a body already on disk. Market.buy now reads this node’s own receipt first (paidFor(): the ledger settlement, else the purchase row) and collects on it; `again: true` / `--again` / the web’s "pay a second time" control is the only way to pay twice. Verified live: the second buy leaves the balance untouched, --again still pays, POST /api/patches/:id/buy answers redeemed with total 0.

verified.by: adversarial re-test against a live node (port base 3790, NGRAM_RUNTIME_API=http://127.0.0.1:9)
verified.note: Web half re-tested 2026-09-04 after a real purchase (5 node credit, real tx, through the UI): the Buy tab reads "Already purchased", states what was paid and when with the tx hash, offers "Load into the model" as the primary action, and puts a second payment behind a confirm that names the price and says the earlier tx hash is overwritten. The node-side idempotency is untouched and still open.

items.title: A local-credit payment is consumed on the first request and can never be replayed: after a lost response the buyer is debited and gets nothing
items.problem: `settlePayment` calls `takeNonce` before it checks amount, signature, balance or duplication (market.ts:694-703). Replaying the exact payload that succeeded — what any client does after a timeout — returns `402 {"error":"unknown or expired nonce"}`, not the manifest and not 'already used'; the settle record has already debited the buyer (`creditBalance` derives from settlements, market.ts:670-680). The same ordering means any failed attempt (wrong amount, bad signature, insufficient balance) burns the nonce, and the error never says a fresh `GET` is needed.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-10-local-credit-nonce-replay.txt (step 3 HTTP 200 → step 4, the identical payload, 'unknown or expired nonce'; steps 1-2: 'amount below price' then the same nonce → 'unknown or expired nonce'). Re-read at HEAD: market.ts:694-703.
items.user_cost: Full price lost per timeout, with an error that reads like clock skew. The developer must write their own signed download client to collect what they paid for, and every learning mistake costs a round trip and a nonce.
items.fix: Make the payment idempotent and the nonce consumed last: compute the intent hash first, and if `store.paymentSeen(h)` and the recorded settlement's buyer is `payload.from`, re-issue a manifest with no new settle (see 273); validate amount, signature and balance before `takeNonce`; add `"single_use": true` to the requirement and phrase the error as 'nonce … was consumed by an earlier attempt — GET the resource again for a new quote'.
items.fixed_note: settlePayment validates amount, nonce, signature and balance BEFORE it spends the nonce, so a rejected attempt no longer burns the quote; a nonce that a settlement did consume answers 'nonce … was consumed by an earlier attempt — GET <resource> again for a new quote' instead of 'unknown or expired nonce', and the requirement says `single_use: true`. Verified live: an under-payment and a bad signature on one nonce, then the correct payment on that same nonce → 200. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — a bad signature and an under-price attempt both left the nonce spendable, and the good payment on that same nonce went through.

items.title: A buyer who paid but lost the manifest has a working recovery path that no screen, command or document mentions — the seller answers 'payment already used'
items.surface: `GET /x402/patch/:id` replay; `GET /p2p/blob/:sha` with `x-ngram-auth`; Buy tab error alert
items.problem: `settlePayment` refuses a second presentation of the same payment (market.ts:699, 706) and never re-issues the manifest to the recorded buyer. Yet `mayDownload` admits any address with a settlement for that sha (market.ts:651), so the body is still collectable — with a signed `x-ngram-auth` header and no token. Neither `market.buy` nor the agent ever takes that path (both throw at market.ts:788 / agent.ts:214), no CLI verb exposes it, and the Buy tab prints `errorMessage(error)` (PatchPage.tsx:535).
items.evidence: critic-01-recover-blob-signed.txt (settled buyer node-b, signed header, no token → HTTP 200, 3,854,446 bytes, from the seller and from a peer holder; a stranger gets 402); p2p-trust-12-replay-used-payment.txt (the payer's own replay → 402 'payment already used'). Code at HEAD: market.ts:651, 699, 706.
items.user_cost: The buyer has paid, the seller has the money and the settle record, and the product's only sentence to them is 'payment already used'. The one honest next step exists in the code and is invisible; the visible next step (Buy again) charges again.
items.fix: On presentation of a payment already settled for this patch and this buyer, re-issue the manifest (idempotent redemption) instead of rejecting it. Add `ainize patch download <id>` and a Buy-tab action 'You paid on <date> — download again (free)' that uses the signed `/p2p/blob` path, and document that path in /docs and openapi.ts (288).
items.fixed_note: A payment presented again by the payer is redeemed again — same settlement, fresh manifest, `x-payment-response {replayed:true}`, no second charge — and only a stranger's replay is refused. The recovery path has a name now: `ainize patch download <id>` / POST /api/patches/:id/collect re-presents the recorded payment, or fetches the body over the signed /p2p/blob path the settlement already unlocks, and the Buy tab's 'no free re-download exists' warning is now a 'Download again (free)' button. Verified live: manifest re-issued after a dropped response, and a forgotten 3.9 MB body collected back, with one settle record throughout. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — the payer replayed the identical X-PAYMENT and got the manifest back with x-payment-response {replayed:true} and no second charge.

items.title: The money moves before anything is written down: a failure between the transfer and the manifest leaves an irreversible payment that neither the node nor the agent recorded
items.problem: In `market.buy` the AIN transfer happens at market.ts:781, the throw on a bad response at market.ts:788, and `putPurchase` only at market.ts:812 — a failure in between leaves a settled sale on the ledger and no row on the buyer's node. In the agent, `payFor` transfers first and assigns `res.tx_hash` only after a 200 (agent.ts:141, 214); the catch in packages/agent/src/bin.ts:53-56 prints `agent failed: …` and exits 1 with no JSON, and nothing is written under `~/.ngram-agent`. A second run makes a second transfer.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-05-partial-failure-tx-lost.txt (proxy answers 503 to the retry; 196.5 → 196.3 AIN over two attempts; `ls ~/.ngram-agent` shows identity.json and patches/ only); code at HEAD: market.ts:781-812, agent.ts:141-214.
items.user_cost: The evidence needed to recover or dispute a lost payment exists only on the chain, and only if you know to scrape `/transfer/<me>/<seller>/`. On a 25 AIN item each attempt is a real loss.
items.fix: Write the intent before the money: log `paid tx <hash> → <payTo> for <resource> (nonce …)` and append it to `<home>/pending-payments.jsonl` (agent) / a `pending_payments` row (node) BEFORE the retry; on the next run re-present a pending payment instead of transferring again; with `--json` print the partial result with `error` and `tx_hash` and exit non-zero.
items.fixed_note: The intent is written before the money: a `pending_payments` row exists from the moment the node has a quote, carries the tx hash the instant the transfer returns and is only marked settled when a manifest is in hand; the next buy re-presents that payment instead of paying again, the buy error names the row and `ainize patch download`, and GET /api/me/pending-payments shows what is owed. The agent does the same in <home>/pending-payments.jsonl and prints the partial result with `--json` (error, tx hash, pending file) instead of one red line. Verified live against a proxy that settled upstream and dropped the response: two runs, one settle record, one body, on both the node and the agent path. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — after deleting the body, `ainize patch download` collected it on the recorded settlement with no new payment and the seller-side balance did not move.

items.title: A node that changes its port loses every listing it ever published: the gateway URL is frozen in the immutable anchor and nothing re-points it
items.problem: `announce` writes `gateway_url = ${this.publicUrl}/x402/patch/${id}` into the anchor (market.ts:443) and anchors are immutable (market.ts:374). `market.buy` fetches that URL (market.ts:766) and the catalogue never checks liveness. A node that moves — a new port, a new host, a new tunnel, a container reschedule — keeps the same identity and the same peers, and every one of its knowledges stays LISTED and sellable in every catalogue while every purchase fails.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/critique4-04-node-moved-gateway-frozen.txt (node-d publishes ux4-moving on :3692, restarts on :3693, answers `/api/info` as the same address; node-c's `patch ls` still says LISTED 6 CREDIT; `patch buy ux4-moving` → `error: fetch failed`; the anchor still says gateway http://localhost:3692/…, status LISTED, sellable true).
items.user_cost: A seller loses their whole catalogue permanently for changing a port, and can only recover by republishing every item under new ids — which then supersedes the originals and restarts verification. Buyers see a shop that is open and cannot be entered.
items.fix: Resolve the gateway at buy time instead of trusting the anchor: prefer the peer-table endpoint for `anchor.author` (`store.listPeers()` / `ledger.nodes()`), fall back to `anchor.gateway_url`, and treat the anchor field as a hint. Add an `endpoint` record kind (or reuse the node record, already keyed by address) that a node re-publishes on start, and show 'seller last seen …' on the Buy tab (276). Add `ainize patch relist <id>` for the case where the identity itself changed.
items.fixed_note: gatewaysFor() resolves the seller from the peer table and the node records, tries the candidates in order, and the frozen address on the record is the last of them. VERIFIED LIVE by moving a publisher from :3895 to :3896 after it announced: the buy went through the peer entry and the dead frozen URL was never reached. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK added the two surfaces that still printed the frozen address (requires[] in the 402 and the quote, and elsewhere[] in the chat picker) — c54a8e2.

items.title: A seller that is offline is still 'For sale' everywhere, and buying ends in a bare 'fetch failed' — while three peers hold the body and none may sell it
items.surface: Explore cards; `patch ls`; Buy tab; `ainize use` / `patch buy`; `ainize-agent run`
items.problem: Catalogue status is derived from the ledger only (packages/core/src/catalog.ts:125-165) with no liveness input, although the peer table knows `last_seen` (`ainize nodes` prints it). `market.buy`'s first fetch has no try/catch (market.ts:766) so Node's TypeError 'fetch failed' passes through to the CLI and the web alert; with a 30 s timeout the message is 'The operation was aborted due to timeout'. Only the author's node may sell: `api.ts:933` answers `409 not sold here; gateway is …` to every other holder.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-28-parent-node-unreachable.txt (A down: `patch ls` LISTED, Buy tab 'Buy · 9 node credit', alert 'fetch failed', CLI exit 1); chain-buy-agent-16-author-offline.txt (`agent failed: fetch failed`, node-a and node-b both hold the body); incentives-network-ns-15 (30 s timeout text).
items.user_cost: The buyer cannot tell a dead seller from a broken product or a wrong URL, retries, and — inside a family — may already have paid another node for the child. A network of peers that all hold the file can sell none of it.
items.fix: Probe the gateway origin (`GET <origin>/p2p/info`, 3 s) and the peer's `last_seen` before rendering Buy and before `step('quorum')`; render 'Seller node-a is unreachable (last seen 12:07) — nothing was charged. Held by node-b, node-c, but only the author can sell it.' Map `fetch failed`/`ECONNREFUSED`/timeout in `patchBuy` and the agent to that sentence, and put an 'offline' chip on Explore cards whose seller failed the last N gossip rounds. Longer term: let a holder settle on the author's behalf against an author-signed price quote.
items.fixed_note: market.sellerLiveness() answers from the peer table who the seller is, when it was last seen and which peers hold the body, and both "no gateway" and "the gateway did not answer" now end in one sentence: `A — the seller of law-kr-2026 — is not answering (last seen …), so nothing was bought and nothing was charged. The body is also on C, but only the author's node can sell it…`. Verified end to end on a throwaway 3-node cluster with the seller's listener taken down. The Explore-card "offline" chip is web-side (another workstream's files) and is not part of this.

items.title: Free knowledge is not free to obtain: price 0 runs the whole payment ceremony, needs a funded identity and writes a public sale record
items.surface: `GET /x402/patch/:id` on a price-0 anchor; `ainize patch buy`; the teach node's 74 free lessons
items.problem: `api.ts:940-944` answers 402 whenever there is no `X-PAYMENT` header, whatever the price, and `requirementsFor` mints a nonce for `maxAmountRequired: "0"`. The buyer must have an identity, sign an intent, and the seller appends a settle record naming them. `market.buy`'s free branch (`else if (r1.ok) step('free', 'no payment required')`, market.ts:797-799) is dead code. On node-u 74 of 136 published lessons are priced 0.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/critique4-01-free-is-not-free.txt (402 with `maxAmountRequired "0"`; `✓ bought ux4-free for 0 (local-credit)` with a signed intent; `ledger ls --kind settle` → 'ux4-free · 0 CREDIT · buyer 0x8186…B3E2'; the seller's wallet lists a 0 CREDIT sale).
items.user_cost: The cheapest on-ramp into the sharing economy — take a free lesson, try it, build on it — costs a wallet, a signature and a permanent public record of who took it. A visitor cannot do it at all (buying is operator-only), and 'free' items pad every sold/revenue/popular figure with 0-value sales.
items.fix: In the gateway, when `Number(price) === 0` return the manifest to any signed requester (or any requester, recording `scheme:'free'`) with no nonce and no settlement, and count it as a download rather than a sale; keep the buyer's address out of the record unless they paid. Make the Buy tab and `patch ls` say 'Free — no payment needed' instead of 'Buy · 0 node credit'.

items.title: A price can never be changed: no discount, no raise, no 'make it free' — the only re-pricing is a new anchor that retires the old one
items.problem: Anchors are immutable (`updateDraft` → 'only drafts can be edited (anchors are immutable on the ledger)', market.ts:374) and there is no verb anywhere — the `patch` command tree has publish/announce/verify/challenge/buy/apply/remove/conflicts/records/rm/forget and nothing about price (packages/cli/src/bin.ts:188-236). A seller who priced a first listing at the 0.1 default, or who wants to run a launch discount, or who wants to make an obsolete knowledge free, has no path but republishing — which supersedes their own item, restarts verification and splits the sales history.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/critique4-03-price-is-immutable.txt (`PATCH /api/patches/ux4-paid {"price":"4"}` as the logged-in operator → `only drafts can be edited (anchors are immutable on the ledger)`; the same for the free item; `patch --help` has no price verb).
items.user_cost: Every price is a one-shot guess made before a single sale, on a market whose own publish form gives no pricing guidance (item 162). Sellers cannot respond to demand, to a cheaper copy of their file (363), or to a superseding version.
items.fix: Add a `price` record kind (`{patch_id, price, currency, at, sig}`) that only the anchor's author may write, have `deriveCatalog` fold the newest one into the entry, and read it in `requirementsFor`/`settlePayment` so the quote and the charge move together; expose `ainize patch price <id> <price>` and a price field on the Manage page, and show a price history on the knowledge page so a buyer can see a discount is real.

items.title: An AIN transfer below the price is neither credited nor refunded: the seller keeps it and the buyer is told only 'transfer 0.1 below price 5'
items.problem: `settlePayment` rejects a short transfer (market.ts:709) without calling `markPayment`, so the AIN stays in the seller's wallet, no settlement exists, and the tx hash remains spendable — for any of that seller's items priced at or below the amount, by anyone (344). Prices are strings like '0.1' and '25' and the agent transfers `Number(req.maxAmountRequired)` with no comparison against the anchor (290).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-02-replay-theft-wrongamount.txt (section E4: `transfer 0.1 below price 5`, money not returned, no settlement written).
items.user_cost: A rounding or typing mistake donates the transfer to the seller with no receipt, no credit and no instruction; the rule is learned by losing money.
items.fix: Either accept several transfers under one `transfer_key` and settle when their sum reaches the price, or answer `{error, received, missing, transfer_key, refund_policy}` and record a `credit` row the buyer can top up; document the behaviour in /docs. In the agent and `market.buy`, compare `req.maxAmountRequired` with `anchor.price` before transferring.

items.title: The buyer's receipt never shows who was paid, although the seller returns the full split in the same response
items.surface: `ainize patch buy` / `use` receipt; Buy-tab PurchaseTimeline; Dashboard 'Purchased knowledge'; History tab
items.problem: The gateway sets `x-payment-response: {settled, tx, royalty:{…}}` (api.ts:951) and `market.buy` keeps only `x-payment-tx-hash` (market.ts:790); `PurchaseResult` has no royalty field and `putPurchase` stores amount/scheme/manifest/path (market.ts:812). So the CLI prints `✓ bought pixel-child for 3 (local-credit)`, the web receipt prints the timeline and hashes, the History row says '… purchase settled · 3 node credit · buyer 0x…' (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/detail.ts:32) — while the settle record on every node carries `{node-a: 0.9, node-b: 2.1}`. The one place the split is rendered is the seller's own Logs page (LogsPage.tsx:79-83).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-06-cli-buy-child.txt (receipt vs settle record); seller-royalties-anc-02-buy-chain-x402.txt (headers carry node-c 3 + 1.5, node-b 1.5, seller 14); critic-03-nodeb-rebuy-pixelplus.txt (six steps, no payees). Earlier reviews cover the quote side (item 236) and the ledger row (item 197), not the buyer's receipt.
items.user_cost: The product's central promise to the buyer — 'Revenue is split automatically with the original creators' — is never demonstrated at the moment it happens, so there is no reason to believe the next sentence, and no way to check that the lineage shown on the page was honoured.
items.fix: Parse `x-payment-response` in `market.buy`, store `royalty` on the purchase row, return it in `PurchaseResult`, and print `3 CREDIT → node-b 2.1 (seller) · node-a 0.9 (creator of pixel-parent)` in the CLI receipt, the web timeline (PatchPage.tsx:542-559) and an expandable column of the Purchased table. Compute the same table from `royaltySplit` in the 402 body and the Buy tab so it is visible before paying, and put the licence there too.

items.title: A family is loaded in whatever order it was bought, and the base can land on top of its own derivative
items.surface: `ainize use`; `branch subscribe`; the 20 s watchdog; Dashboard 'In model'
items.problem: `subscribe` applies `b.patch_ids` in list order (market.ts:1105-1112), `buy({apply})` applies one id, and the watchdog re-applies per patch (market.ts:745-757); the runtime is last-wins on shared rows and the `applied` table has no order column. The design records this as F5 (docs/lineage-teach-design.md:23) and L1's `base.stack` (types.ts:170-176) now states the intended order on the record — nothing reads it.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-15-node-d-chain.txt ('applied order on node-d: [grandchild, child, parent]' with reason `subscription:chain/pixel`); chain-buy-human-26-buyer-d-dashboard-en-1280.png ('In model: yes' ×3, no order).
items.user_cost: A buyer pays for three knowledges and can get the behaviour of the base alone; nothing on any screen hints at it, and a runtime restart can reshuffle it again. Because today's children contain their base's rows, 'parent last' really does overwrite the child's values.
items.fix: Order applies by lineage depth (ancestors first) in `subscribe`, in `buy({apply})` and in the watchdog (sort `listApplied()` by depth, or by `base.stack` when present); store `position` on the applied row; show 'Loaded in order: pixel-parent → pixel-child' on the Dashboard and in `ainize status`; refuse `removePatch` of a parent while a child is applied.
items.fixed_note: `resolveStack` orders by declared lineage as well as by `base.stack`: `orderByLineage` is a stable topological pass over the parents of the knowledges actually being loaded, so a family bought newest-first is loaded oldest-first. Nothing is fetched that was not asked for, two independent bases keep the caller's order, and a cycle leaves the order untouched. Every loader goes through it (`patch apply`, `use --bundle`, `branch subscribe`, the watchdog's re-assert). Covered by test/lineage-order.test.ts (5 cases, no model). The 'Loaded in order' line was already on the Dashboard and in `ainize status`, and `removePatch` already refuses to pull a base out from under a loaded add-on.

items.title: Nothing on the browse surfaces says a knowledge is an add-on: the family is invisible exactly where prices are compared
items.surface: Explore cards; `ainize patch ls`; `ainize-agent catalog`; the 402 `description`
items.problem: No component under packages/web/src/components/public/ mentions parents or lineage; `patch ls` columns are ID/STATUS/AUTHOR/MODEL/ROWS/SIZE/PRICE/ATTEST/SOLD/BENCHMARK (packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:25-36); the agent's catalogue row prints id/status/rows/price/attest/name (packages/agent/src/bin.ts:64); the 402 description is `Knowledge patch <id> (<rows> rows, <model>)` (market.ts:661).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-13-explore-C-en-1280.png (the child and grandchild read as ordinary 3- and 2-credit items; the only 'derivative' wording came from the publisher's own `--description`); teach-triggered-12-lesson-402.txt.
items.user_cost: A buyer choosing between a 5-credit base and a 3-credit item built on it has no way to tell which is which until the fourth tab of the detail page — and an agent, which never opens a page, cannot tell at all.
items.fix: Add a chip to the card and a BUILT ON column to `patch ls` / `agent catalog` from `lineage.parents` + `derivation.kind` ('Add-on to pixel-parent' / 'Includes its base'), and put `built on <id>` plus `requires[]` into the 402 description and body (270).
items.shipped: WEB HALF ONLY (cd59b61). The Explore and /benchmarks cards carry the family: "Add-on · runs on <base>" when anchor.base.stack is set (it does not work without that base underneath) or "Built on <parent>" when it only declares parents, each with a plain-language explanation reachable by tap and by keyboard. Still open: the BUILT ON column on `ainize patch ls` and `ainize-agent catalog`, and `built on <id>` plus requires[] in the 402 description and body — an agent still cannot tell.
items.progress_note: The web half is closed — the browse card carries an Add-on / Built-on chip from `base.stack` and `parents`. Left: the BUILT ON column on `ainize patch ls` and `ainize-agent catalog` (cli/commands/patch.ts and packages/agent, held by the terminal workstream this pass) and `built on <id>` in the 402 description (market.requirementsFor, held by the money workstream).

items.title: The child that contains every row of its base is labelled 'Different subject — overlapping entries need reconciling', ten lines under 'Origins'
items.problem: `PatchPage.tsx:439-441` chooses `detail.lin.rel_other` whenever the two schemas differ, with no check that the overlap partner is a declared parent; the same page has just drawn that knowledge as the origin. Nothing on the page states the one fact a buyer needs — 2,992 of 2,992 rows are the base's — although `blobs.addrSet` already computes it and L1's `derivation.added_rows/changed_rows` (types.ts:159-166) is designed to carry it.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-07-child-visitor-notes.json ('pixel-parent · 2,992 memory entries · Different subject — overlapping entries need reconciling' under 'Origins → pixel-parent'); chain-buy-human-17-child-while-parent-challenged-en-1280-lineage.png; teach-triggered-27-lesson3-page-en-1280.png ('2,992 Memory entries · 1 Facts').
items.user_cost: The page that decides whether the buyer must also buy the base contradicts itself; the ancestor is undercut by a copy of their own rows and the buyer is told the two are unrelated.
items.fix: When an overlap partner is in `anchor.parents`, replace the relation text with 'contains {n} of its base's {total} entries — you do not need pixel-parent' (or 'adds {k} on top of its base'), sourced from `derivation` when present and from the address-set intersection otherwise; add the same line to the Buy tab and refuse to list a child whose body is ≥95 % its parent unless it declares `derivation.kind: 'update'`.
items.fixed_note: Under the relation the row now states the arithmetic, from the partner's own row count in the same-subject list this page already loads: "This knowledge already covers all 241,992 of its entries, so it does not have to be loaded as well" for the contained base, and "2,170 of its 2,992 entries are also here — the other 822 are not in this knowledge" for pixelplus-087600. The Buy tab's "Needs underneath it" row names a covered origin by name and says that base does not have to be bought. RESIDUE, node: refusing to list a child whose body is ≥95 % its parent unless it declares derivation.kind 'update'.

items.title: `ainize-agent run` reports SUCCESS and exit 0 when the knowledge was never loaded, and its defaults point at another machine's GPU
items.problem: The no-runtime branch prints `[6] no runtime (/nonexistent) — apply step skipped; body kept at …`, then sets `success: true` and `result: SUCCESS — the 402 purchase loop completed`; bin.ts exits 0. `--api` defaults to `http://localhost:8000` and `--repo` to `/mnt/newdata/qwen3.8` — one developer's machine, and on this host :8000 is the production server this review was forbidden to touch.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-01-agent-run-ain.txt; chain-buy-agent-05-partial-failure-tx-lost.txt; code at HEAD agent.ts:271-273, bin.ts:38-41.
items.user_cost: Automation keyed on the exit code believes knowledge is live when it is only on disk — and pays again next run (271). Anyone else's machine silently takes the skipped path on every run.
items.fix: Exit 0 only when applied (or `--download-only` was passed); otherwise exit 3 with `downloaded, NOT loaded: no runtime at <repo>`. Read `api`/`repo` from the market node's `/api/info.runtime` when not given and refuse to run against a silent default.
items.fixed_note: A run that ends with the body on disk and nothing in any model is `downloaded`, not SUCCESS: exit 3 with `downloaded, NOT loaded` and the command that would load it, or 0 with `--download-only`. `--api` and `--repo` already had no machine-specific defaults (item 230); the run prints which serving API it resolved and from where. Verified by test (outcome and exit code) — the loaded path itself needs a model server (deferred).

items.title: On an AIN market `ainize-agent balance` prints '100 CREDIT' while the wallet holds 196 AIN, and the funding hint names a command that only works on a local dev chain
items.problem: `balance` always derives a local-credit figure from settle records and never reads `/api/info.ledger.kind` or `AinLedger.balance()` (packages/agent/src/bin.ts:64-77); the run-time hint is `fund it: ngram chain fund 0x…` (agent.ts:140) — the binary is `ainize` and `chainFund` refuses non-local providers (packages/cli/src/commands/chain.ts:103-112).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-03-agent-errors-balance.txt ('100 CREDIT (initial credit 100 …)' against node-a whose ledger is `ain` and whose wallet holds 196.5 AIN).
items.user_cost: A developer budgeting a chain of purchases cannot ask the agent what it can spend, and the wrong number is presented with confidence; the recovery instruction is a dead end on any real network.
items.fix: Read `/api/info.ledger.kind`: for `ain` print `AinLedger.balance()` in AIN, label CREDIT output as local-only, and print `ainize chain fund <addr>` only when the provider host is local, otherwise 'send AIN to <addr> on <network>'.
items.fixed_note: `agent balance` reads /api/info.ledger.kind: on an AIN market it answers with AinLedger.balance() in AIN, on a local one it labels CREDIT as this node's own development credit and says who issues it; the funding hint is `ainize chain fund <addr>` only when the AIN provider is local, otherwise 'send AIN to <addr> on <network>', and the same rule now writes payFor's out-of-funds message (which said `ngram chain fund`, a binary that does not exist and a command that refuses a real network). It also prints what the agent has spent today. Verified live against a local-ledger node; the AIN branch needs a chain (deferred).

items.title: An agent's purchases leave no receipt it can read back: nothing on disk, no on-chain access receipt, no `purchases` command, no buyer filter on the ledger
items.problem: The agent writes `identity.json` and `patches/<sha>.npz` and nothing else; `recordAccess` (the on-chain access receipt) is called only from `market.buy` (market.ts:815-817), so an agent's purchases leave no chain receipt; `GET /api/ledger` accepts `since/kind/limit` only (api.ts:224-231) — there is no `buyer=` filter, and the seller's ledger is the only place the sale exists.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-08-private-leaf-buy-royalty.txt (§H); today's count on the demo: 187 settle records from one agent identity readable only from node-a's ledger.
items.user_cost: An operator auditing spend, or an automation deciding what it already owns, must scrape every seller's ledger by hand — impossible on a network with many sellers, and the direct cause of the repeat payments in 271.
items.fix: Append `{patch_id, sha256, seller, amount, currency, scheme, tx_hash, nonce, manifest, path, at}` to `<home>/purchases.jsonl` on every settled payment; add `ainize-agent purchases [--json]`; call `recordAccess` for agent purchases too; add `buyer=`/`seller=` filters to `GET /api/ledger`.
items.fixed_note: Every settled purchase is appended to `<home>/purchases.jsonl` with patch id, sha256, seller, seller name, gateway, market, amount, currency, scheme, tx hash and path, and `ainize-agent purchases [--json]` reads them back with today's spend. Verified by test. The two node-side halves of the reviewer's fix — calling recordAccess for agent purchases and a `buyer=` filter on GET /api/ledger — are in the money group's region and stay open.

items.title: There is no way to automate 'keep these knowledges loaded and current': the agent is one-shot, restores by default, records nothing, and decides what to buy by probing a shared model
items.problem: The agent has run/catalog/balance/keys only. Each run re-asks the model and buys when the answer is wrong (agent.ts:160-167) — on a shared runtime that answer belongs to whoever else loaded something; `--keep` leaves the patch applied with no local record, no watchdog and no version tracking; newer versions are noticed only via `--follow-latest`, which pays again (271). Track subscription exists only for nodes, and is broken (357).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-01-agent-run-ain.txt (first run 'correct — nothing to buy' because another tenant's patch was loaded; second run bought); `ainize-agent --help` in chain-buy-agent-03.
items.user_cost: The product's stated audience — agents that buy knowledge automatically — must write their own scheduler, ownership ledger and version watcher, and any naive cron of `agent run` is a repeat-purchase loop.
items.fix: Add `ainize-agent watch --patch a,b,c --budget-per-day N [--follow-latest]`: keep a local manifest of owned patches (286), apply them on start, re-apply after a runtime restart (poll `/v1/models`), follow supersede marks within budget, and decide from the purchase record — never from probing a shared model.
items.fixed_note: `ainize-agent watch --patch a,b --track daily/krx --budget-per-day N [--interval|--once]` keeps a set current: it decides what it owns from its own receipts and never by probing a shared model, buys only what is missing, refuses a purchase that would take the day over budget, follows supersede marks under the same budget, reports per cycle what it did, and re-loads the watched set when a serving model comes back after an outage (only with an explicit --repo; without one it loads nothing and says so). Verified by test: over_budget → bought → owned across three cycles, with one settlement on the seller's ledger.

items.title: The payment protocol a third-party client must implement is four sentences; every rule that costs money is learned by losing money
items.surface: /docs 'Automatic payment flow'; the Buy tab curl example; packages/node/src/openapi.ts
items.problem: `docs.x402.steps` (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/docs.ts:31) is four numbered sentences; the Buy tab's copy-paste example sends `{"scheme":"ain-transfer","network":"ain:local","txHash":"0x…"}` and works only because the server validates nothing else (344); `X402Requirement` in openapi.ts:28-29 omits `description` and `transfer_key`, there is no schema for `x-payment-response`, and 409/503 are undocumented. Nowhere is it written that the local-credit nonce is single-use and burnt by a failed attempt, that quotes expire in 10 minutes (and are not enforced on the AIN path), that 'payment already used' is final, that 423 means a challenge, or that `billing: per_download` means every fetch is a new sale.
items.evidence: docs.ts:31; chain-buy-agent-07-web-buytab-child-en-1280.png; chain-buy-agent-10-local-credit-nonce-replay.txt; chain-buy-agent-02-replay-theft-wrongamount.txt.
items.user_cost: Each undocumented rule cost this review a nonce, a request cycle or 0.1 AIN; a company integrating against a real chain pays the same tuition with real money.
items.fix: Add a 'Payment protocol' section to /docs and openapi.ts: per scheme the exact payload with every field, the state machine (402 → pay → retry → 200 | reasons), nonce/expiry/idempotency rules, every status code, the response headers, the token lifetime and the billing semantics — and keep the curl example correct once the server validates the fields.
items.fixed_note: The protocol is written down in docs/{en,ko}/reference/x402.md — state machine, every status, nonce/expiry/idempotency, the receipt headers, the 24-hour token, per_download semantics and a table of every refusal, all measured against a running node. The openapi.ts schema fields and the Buy tab's curl example are node and knowledge-page work.

items.title: The buyer's own purchase row names no seller: their node cannot answer 'who did I pay for this?'
items.problem: `putPurchase` stores `{patch_id, sha256, tx_hash, scheme, amount, manifest, path, created_at}` (market.ts:812) — no seller address, no gateway, no royalty. The Dashboard columns are Paid / tx / file / loaded / actions (packages/web/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:189-193). The seller is recoverable only by re-deriving the catalogue, which fails once the seller's anchor is gone from this node's view.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-26-buyer-d-dashboard-en-1280.png; code at HEAD market.ts:812, DashboardPage.tsx:189-193.
items.user_cost: The only durable record of a purchase on the buyer's side omits the counterparty — the first thing anyone needs for a refund request, a dispute (347) or an audit.
items.fix: Store `seller`, `seller_name`, `gateway_url` and the parsed `royalty` on the purchase row and show a 'Paid to' column (and `ainize wallet` line) beside the amount.
items.fixed_note: The buyer can answer 'who did I pay for this?': `ainize purchases` resolves the seller (name and address) from the anchor the same call returns, beside the amount, the tx, the file and the stack position, and the agent's own purchases.jsonl stores `seller` and `seller_name` on every row. Storing the seller on the node's `purchases` table itself, and the Dashboard column, are in the money group's region (market.putPurchase / DashboardPage).

items.title: `--max-price` is checked against the catalogue price, but the agent pays whatever amount the 402 asks for
items.problem: The guard compares `pick.anchor.price` with `--max-price` (agent.ts:188); `payFor` then transfers `Number(req.maxAmountRequired)` from the 402 (agent.ts:141) with no comparison to the anchor or the budget, and does not check that `req.payTo` is the anchor's author. `market.buy` has the same shape (market.ts:781).
items.evidence: Code read at HEAD: agent.ts:141, 188; market.ts:781. The gateway is a separate HTTP endpoint run by the seller, so quote and anchor can differ.
items.user_cost: The one safety flag the agent offers does not bound the transfer it actually makes.
items.fix: After decoding the 402, refuse when `Number(req.maxAmountRequired) > min(anchor.price, maxPrice)` or `req.payTo !== anchor.author`, and print the mismatch.
items.fixed_note: `checkRequirement` runs before any transfer: the 402 may not ask for more than the anchor's price, may not exceed --max-price, and may not name a payee other than the anchor's author (a payment to anyone else buys nothing). Verified by test for all three refusals and the case-insensitive accept.

items.title: `--follow-latest` re-targets the purchase to an item 250× the price, and only an explicit budget stops it
items.problem: `resolveSupersedes` follows supersede marks to the newest LISTED patch; the switch line says 'newer patch on the same benchmark' and names no price (agent.ts:106); the price guard runs only when `--max-price` was given (agent.ts:188). pixelplus-087600 (0.1 AIN) is superseded by krx-all-2761 (25 AIN); unattended, the agent pays 25.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-03-agent-errors-balance.txt (with `--max-price 0.1` it refuses; without, it pays 25 — the following `candidate:` line does print the new price).
items.user_cost: An automation told to 'stay current' spends 250× what it was asked to spend, unattended.
items.fix: Print `0.1 → 25 AIN` on the switch line and default the budget to the originally requested item's price unless `--max-price` raises it; add `--follow-latest=same-price|any`.
items.fixed_note: A supersede switch prints `0.1 → 25 CREDIT` with the newer version's rows and author, and the budget it must fit is the price of the item that was asked for unless --max-price raised it; `--follow-price any` is the explicit opposite and `--no-follow-latest` buys exactly what was named. Verified by test in all three modes.

items.title: With `--json` a failed agent run prints no JSON at all
items.problem: The catch in packages/agent/src/bin.ts:53-56 writes `agent failed: <message>` to stderr and exits 1; the AgentResult (steps, patch_id, scheme, amount, tx_hash) is discarded. In the seller-503 test the JSON run produced nothing on stdout while 0.1 AIN had left the wallet. (The `ainize` CLI has the same defect as item 104; the fix there did not reach this package.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-05-partial-failure-tx-lost.txt.
items.user_cost: An orchestrator cannot tell which step failed or what was already paid, and has to re-parse free text to reconcile spend.
items.fix: Build `res` before the try, attach `error` and `failed_step`, print it as JSON on failure, then exit non-zero.
items.fixed_note: The agent’s catch prints the partial result as JSON under `--json` — `{success:false, error, steps, identity, pending_payments, tx_hash, pending_file}` — so a run that failed after the money moved is still a machine-readable result.

items.title: A seller's refusal reaches the buyer as raw JSON: `payment rejected: 402 {"error":"insufficient credit: 2 < 5"}`
items.surface: `ainize use` / `patch buy`; the Buy-tab error alert
items.problem: `market.buy` throws `payment rejected: ${r2.status} ${await r2.text()}` (market.ts:788) and both the CLI and `errorMessage(error)` in the web print it verbatim. The seller's reasons are all readable sentences on the server side ('insufficient credit', 'transfer not found / not executed', 'this node does not sell that patch') and arrive as a status code plus a JSON blob.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-16-node-e-insufficient.txt; chain-buy-human-17-challenged-parent.txt line 1.
items.user_cost: At the moment a purchase fails, the buyer is shown a stack-trace-shaped string instead of what to do next.
items.fix: Map the seller's error codes to sentences naming the seller, the balance and the price ('node-a refused the payment: your balance is 2 CREDIT and pixel-parent costs 5'), and return the timeline `steps` with the thrown error so `patchBuy` can print where it stopped.
items.fixed_note: A seller's refusal is a sentence naming the seller, the balance and the price ('node-a refused the payment: this agent has 2 CREDIT and pixel-parent costs 5'), with the seller's own code unwrapped from the JSON body — in the agent (as a `REJECTED` step in the timeline as well) and in `ainize patch buy`, which maps insufficient credit, an unconfirmed transfer, a knowledge the seller does not sell and anything else. Verified by test for the five shapes. Returning the timeline `steps` with the thrown error is node-side (market.buy) and stays with the money group.

items.title: Rejected purchases leave 'pay: signed credit intent …' in the buyer's own audit trail, indistinguishable from money that moved
items.problem: `step('pay', …)` is logged before the seller answers (market.ts:783-786) and the `!r2.ok` branch throws without a step or event (market.ts:788). node-e's feed shows three 'pay' lines for purchases that never settled, separable from the one that did only by the absence of a later 'settled' line.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-16-node-e-insufficient.txt (events 'pay: signed credit intent dcb9de…', '669f2d…', '1175a9…' with no settle).
items.user_cost: The local record — the only one besides the wallet — errs in the direction of 'paid'; on AIN the same step precedes a real transfer, so the two cases cannot be told apart afterwards.
items.fix: Log the intent as `pay: prepared …`, add an explicit `rejected: <seller error>` step and event when `r2` is not ok, and include both in the returned/thrown `steps`.
items.fixed_note: `pay` said the same thing whether the money had moved or not and a refusal wrote nothing at all, so a buyer's feed showed three `pay` lines for three failed purchases. An AIN transfer now reads `sent — the seller has not answered yet`, a credit intent `prepared — nothing is spent until the seller accepts it`, and a refusal is its own `rejected` step naming the seller and their reason, in the timeline and in the node log. Committed as a single hunk in market.buy (the money group's file) because no other group owns this finding; nothing else in that file was touched.

items.title: On a phone the price line breaks mid-word: 'pay o / nce per download', 'developm / ent play money'
items.surface: Knowledge page → Buy tab at 360 px
items.problem: `KeyValue`'s `dd` uses `word-break: break-all` against a max-content `dt` column (packages/web/src/components/ui/Misc.tsx:55-59), so at 360 px the money line, the seller address and the gateway URL all break inside words.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-15-grandchild-operator-d-en-360-buy.png; chain-buy-human-08-child-operator-en-360-buy.png.
items.user_cost: The money line of the page is the least readable element on the device most visitors use, and a buyer of a family reads it three times.
items.fix: Below 480 px stack the `dl` (dt above dd, full width) and keep `word-break: normal` with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` only on the URL.
items.fixed_note: KeyValue traded `word-break: break-all` for `overflow-wrap: anywhere` and stacks label-above-value below 480 px, so at 360 px the Buy tab's money line, seller address and gateway URL wrap at word boundaries instead of reading "memory en / tries" and "does not ha / ve to be bought". A hash or a URL still wraps; /network and /ledger gained the same.

items.title: An origin that is CHALLENGED or SUPERSEDED looks perfectly healthy in the web Origins tree — the status is a hover title, and the 402 never mentions a replacement
items.problem: `PatchPage.tsx:449` renders each parent as `<TreeNode title={p.status}>` — a tooltip, invisible on touch — while the CLI prints `parents : pixel-parent (SUPERSEDED)` / `(CHALLENGED)` in plain sight. The lineage payload carries no `superseded_by` for a parent, and `requirementsFor` (market.ts:655-666) has no note, so a retired base keeps quoting its old price with nothing pointing at the current version.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-17-child-while-parent-challenged-en-1280-lineage.png (parent shown with no status while `patch ls` says CHALLENGED); chain-buy-human-27-superseded-parent.txt (child's tree unchanged, `GET /x402/patch/pixel-parent` still 402s for 5 CREDIT; `patch get` on the CLI does say SUPERSEDED).
items.user_cost: The buyer completing a family a day later pays for a retired base and is never pointed at the current one; a buyer of an add-on cannot see that its foundation is under dispute.
items.fix: Add `status` and `superseded_by` to each entry of `lineage.parents`, render them as visible chips in the Origins tree and as a Buy-tab note ('built on pixel-parent, replaced by pixel-parent-v2 · 9 node credit'), and add the same `note` to the 402 requirement of a SUPERSEDED anchor. Do not gate the child's sale on the parent's status — the child passed its own verification.
items.fixed_note: A retired or challenged origin now shows its status as a chip with a link to its replacement, in the Origins tree and beside the money in the Buy tab; the 402's own note belongs to requirementsFor (group G).

flows.name: B. Purchases triggered by teaching
flows.description: Acquiring a base so you can teach on top of it, and what the teacher is told about price, share and payment.

items.title: To teach on top of a knowledge this node does not hold there is no way to get it: the picker hides it, the CLI says 'unknown knowledge', and a visitor cannot buy at all
items.surface: Live test / Teach knowledge picker; `GET /api/chat/patches`; `ainize teach train --patch <id>`; `POST /api/patches/:id/buy`
items.problem: `testablePatches` returns only entries whose body is already in the blob store (market.ts:1034-1038), so the picker silently omits every knowledge the node has not fetched — no greyed row, no price, no link. `contextTargets` answers `invalid: this node does not hold the body of X` when the anchor is known and `invalid: unknown knowledge X` — the same wording as a typo — when it is not (packages/node/src/teach.ts:559-561); `chat` says 'buy it first' (market.ts:812). Buying is operator-only (`requireOperator` on `/api/patches/:id/buy`, api.ts:330), so a visitor has no way to buy, to request, or even to learn that the knowledge exists elsewhere, and the operator is never told anyone wanted it.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-24-train-on-unheld-body.txt (`error: invalid: this node does not hold the body of pixel-parent-c`); teach-triggered-18-train-on-unknown-id.txt (`error: invalid: unknown knowledge krx-all-2761`); chain-buy-human-24-teach-lineage-price.txt (`/api/chat/patches` on node-e lists only its two purchases).
items.user_cost: The chained purchase the whole product is built around — I want to extend X, so someone buys X — has no first step on screen. Meanwhile a node that verified X holds it for free (327), so the only people asked to acquire a base are those who cannot.
items.fix: Return unheld verified entries from `/api/chat/patches` with `held:false, price, gateway_url` and render them disabled with 'Not on this node — Buy (5 node credit) to test or teach on it'; split `contextTargets`' error into three cases (unknown id / known but not held, with the seller and price / sold elsewhere, with the node URL); add `POST /api/teach/requests {patch_id}` writing a `teach` event and a badge on the operator's Teaching tab ('3 visitors asked to build on pixel-parent-c · Buy 8 CREDIT').
items.fixed_note: GET /api/chat/patches now returns `elsewhere[]`: every knowledge this node's model could run but cannot load, with its price, its seller and the reason (not_held / verify_only), rendered as a disabled row in the picker with Buy for the operator and "ask this node to get it" for a visitor (POST /api/chat/patches/:id/request writes one demand event), and `ainize chat --list` prints the same table. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — a body held only because this node verified it appears under elsewhere[] with reason verify_only, not in items[].

items.title: The teach node that is actually deployed has no verifier peers: 136 lessons, up to 75 hours old, all told 'it goes on sale when 2 agree'
items.problem: The sheet promises 'Announced. Independent verifier nodes are now checking it on the real model; it goes on sale when {quorum} agree' (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/teach.ts:162) without ever reading `/api/info`. node-u has quorum 2, roles [seller, serving] and zero peers, so no attestation can ever arrive and self-attestation does not count (catalog.ts:133-136). The teacher page shows 'Registered · awaiting verification' with no age and no verifier count. (Item 147 reported the CLI publish message; the visitor door and the stranded catalogue are new.)
items.evidence: Live today on :3422: `/api/info` peers 0, counts listed 0 / verifying 136, `/api/nodes` 1 node, anchor ages 46.9–75.4 h, 62 of the 136 carry a CREDIT price; packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-39-nodeu-never-listed.txt; teach-triggered-37-nodeu-teacher-never-listed-en-1280.png.
