items.user_cost: Teachers set a price, consent to a permanent public record and wait for sales that cannot happen. The price/payout/consent ceremony is theatre on the node that is actually deployed for teaching.
items.fix: Before the sheet submits, read `/api/info` (peers with the verifier role vs quorum); if fewer than quorum, replace the price/payout block with 'This node has 0 verifier peers and needs 2 to put anything on sale — your lesson will be recorded but cannot be sold here' and require an explicit 'publish anyway'. On the teacher page and in `teach status`, show 'awaiting verification for 75 h · 0 of 2 verifiers have looked · this node has no verifier peers' from `created_at` and the peer list.
items.fixed_note: GET /api/teach/policy, the publish challenge and the teacher profile now carry `verification {quorum, peers, reachable, verifiers}` (peers that answered a recent p2p round and advertise the verifier role; this node's own attestation is reported separately and never counted). Below quorum the publish sheet replaces the 'goes on sale when 2 agree' promise with what will really happen and requires an explicit 'publish anyway', the done state says it too, and the teacher page and `teach status` show per-lesson waiting time and verifier count. Node/web 473d2bc, CLI 69c17fa. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — GET /api/teach/policy carries verification {quorum, peers, reachable, verifiers, self_verifier} and `teach publish` prints "3 verifier peer(s) reachable — it goes on sale when 2 of them agree".

items.title: On a local-ledger node the teacher prices in play money and is later shown '4.9 CREDIT Paid' for credit a browser key can never spend
items.surface: PublishSheet price field; /teacher/<address> earnings; the payout radio 'My own wallet address'
items.problem: `price.credit_note` ('node credit = development play money (no real value)', packages/web/src/i18n/common.ts:57) is used by the picker, the patch list and the operator surfaces — never by PublishSheet.tsx or TeacherPage.tsx (grep). The sheet says 'Price per download (CREDIT) — 0 = free' and offers an AIN wallet address on a node that settles in credit; the teacher page then reports Owed/Paid and 'settled as node credit' (teach.ts:1799 marks local-credit rows paid unconditionally). `creditBalance` grants every unseen address 100 CREDIT (market.ts:670-680), so 'Paid' is a bookkeeping line on one node's ledger with no spend path.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-05-sheet-text.txt (no play-money note); teach-triggered-17-teacher-after-sale-en-1280.png ('4.9 CREDIT Paid · settled as node credit'); teach-triggered-23-x402-buy-lesson3.txt (a fresh browser key bought the lesson); node-u today: 62 of 136 lessons priced in CREDIT.
items.user_cost: A teacher believes they earned money, entered a wallet address that will receive nothing, and cannot move, spend or verify the number anywhere.
items.fix: When `info.ledger.kind === 'local'`, render `price.credit_note` under the sheet's price field and in the teacher-page header, relabel 'Paid' as 'Credited on node-a (not withdrawable)', and hide or explain the AIN wallet option; on AIN nodes say 'paid as an AIN transfer to {address}' and show the tx hash per row.
items.fixed_note: The publish sheet renders `price.credit_note` under the price field and says where a payout actually lands on a local-ledger node; the teacher page carries the same note and relabels Paid as 'Credited on <node> (not withdrawable)'; `teach status` and `teach publish` print the ledger a price is denominated in. The node reports `ledger {kind, currency}` on the teach policy, the challenge and the teacher profile. Node/web 473d2bc, CLI 69c17fa. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — `teach publish` prints "settles in CREDIT on this node’s own ledger — development play money, not withdrawable", and the sheet renders price.credit_note.

items.title: The 'builds on' tick is eleven words: no rate, no creator's name, no 'forever' — and the trainer never loads the base it credits
items.surface: Live test → Teach basket checkbox (`teach.basket.builds_on`); the policy line above it
items.problem: The checkbox reads 'This builds on the knowledge I have loaded (its creators share in sales)' (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/teach.ts:45) and the policy line above it carries queue and timing but no money. Parents reach the trainer only as contrast samples (`contrast: await this.parentSamples(job)`, teach.ts:1227), so the tick is a permanent royalty declaration with no technical dependency — and the sheet later prints a share that the tick itself changes (301).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-16-basket-en-1280.png / -ko-360.png ('Loaded now: Pixelplus ticker code (parent)' then the bare tick); teach.ts:1222-1236; design F1/F2.
items.user_cost: The creator's biggest revenue decision is made from a label that names neither the rate nor the person; the ancestor's biggest income line depends on a box most people leave unticked because nothing says why they would tick it.
items.fix: Render under the tick, from `/api/teach/policy.shares` and the loaded entries: 'pixel-parent's creator (node-a 0xa4Ab…) will receive 30 % of every sale of this lesson, forever; you keep 49 %, node-a 21 %.' Put the same two numbers on the policy line, and add 'Your lesson is trained on its own — buyers do not need the base' until on-top training ships.
items.fixed_note: Under the tick: who is credited by name, that they are paid for as long as the lesson sells, and both numbers (30 % off the top, the 49 % that leaves the teacher) computed from this node's own shares with royaltySplit's arithmetic — plus the fact that buyers do not need the base loaded.

items.title: 'You receive 70 % of every sale' survives on four surfaces after the publish sheet — the public page tells buyers the data provider gets 70 % of a sale that pays them 49 %
items.surface: READY card; public knowledge page 'Data provider: … (70 %)'; operator Teaching settings; /teacher/<addr>
items.problem: `royaltySplit` pays the lineage pool first and carves the contributor share from the fixed remainder (packages/core/src/catalog.ts:288-296), so a lesson built on a listed knowledge pays 0.7 × 0.7 = 49 %. Item 186 covers the publish sheet; the same raw config number is printed by `teach.res.publish_body` (teach.ts:549), by the knowledge page's `detail.people` ('Data provider: UX4 Teacher (70 %)', packages/web/src/i18n/pages/teach.ts:235 via PatchPage.tsx:175) and by the operator's Teaching settings ('Data-provider share of each sale: 70 % — the rest stays with this node'). Only README.md:60 says '70 % of the node's share'.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-23-x402-buy-lesson3.txt (`royalty {node-c 3, teacher 4.9, node-a 2.1}` on a 10 CREDIT sale); teach-triggered-27-lesson3-page-en-1280.png; teach-triggered-32-dashboard-teaching-en-1280.png.
items.user_cost: The buyer reads a public record naming a share nobody is paid, and the teacher sees 4.9 on the earnings page with no explanation of where the other 2.1 went.
items.fix: Add `effective_share` to the patch detail (computed with `royaltySplit` on a unit sale) and render that everywhere a share is shown; change `op.teach.settings.share` and `teach.res.publish_body` to 'of what is left after the network's creator share', printing both numbers; add a unit test asserting the sheet's figure equals `royaltySplit(entry, map, 10, 0.3)[contributor]`.
items.fixed_note: The result screen prints the share a sale of THIS lesson pays, with the lineage pool taken off the top first and both numbers named; the public page no longer prints a share beside the contributor's name at all.

items.title: Verifying someone's knowledge silently grants the right to host it as a teaching base and sell derivatives — and a licence cannot say no
items.surface: `mayDownload` verifier exemption; `contextTargets`; the publish form's licence field
items.problem: A verifier fetches every announced body (verifier.ts:95) and `mayDownload` keeps it free forever (market.ts:645-656); `contextTargets` accepts any entry whose body is held (teach.ts:555-565), so a verified body becomes a teaching base on that node, and derivatives sell there with the base's creator receiving only the 30 % lineage share. That may be the intended bargain, but no page states it: the publish form's licence is free text (item 161) with no `derivatives` flag, the verifier's operator is not told the role grants it, and the base creator's page shows no purchase by that node.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-15-chain-parent-on-node-c.txt + teach-triggered-23 (node-a verified pixel-parent-c, never bought it, hosted it as a base, sold the derivative and kept 21 %); code at HEAD market.ts:645-656, teach.ts:555-565.
items.user_cost: Creators cannot reason about whether to sell bodies, lineage or both; verifiers do not know what the role entitles them to; and 'no derivatives' cannot be expressed at all.
items.fix: State the rule where the decision is made — the publish form ('verifier nodes will hold this file and may host it as a base for visitor lessons; you receive 30 % of each derivative sale'), the verifier's Teaching tab, and the terms — and replace the free-text licence with the closed list L0 already added (types.ts:99) plus a `derivatives: allowed | credit-only | none` flag that `contextTargets` enforces.
items.fixed_note: `contextTargets` checks `market.hasLicense(entry)` before a knowledge may be used as a teaching base, in the same words as the other four doors (apply, the chat picker, chat, subscribe): a body fetched to score it is possession, never the right to teach on top of it and sell the derivative.

items.title: A one-fact lesson that ships 2,992 of its base's rows is verified 2/2 and sold as new; nothing anywhere counts the rows it did not add
items.surface: Taught lesson page ('2,992 Memory entries · 1 Facts'); verifier attestations; `teach.ts` stub trainer
items.problem: The stub backend copies the fixture body whenever a correction mentions the fixture subject (teach.ts:1375-1388), and no verifier or catalogue field records how much of a child's body is its parents' — L1 added `derivation.added_rows/changed_rows` and `base.pre_state_sha256` to the anchor (types.ts:159-176) but nothing computes or checks them. The page prints both numbers side by side with no comment; the design's own F3 says a real `--init-patch` build is a squash of parent rows plus new rows, so the disclosure matters beyond the stub.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-27-lesson3-page-en-1280.png; teach-triggered-29-manage-lesson3-en-1280.png (overlap 'pixel-parent-c · 2,992 memory entries'); critique4-02-resold-copy-supersedes-the-original.txt (both verifiers PASS a byte-identical body with 'integrity=sha256 ok').
items.user_cost: A buyer pays 10 for what is functionally the 8-credit base plus one fact; the base's creator is paid 30 % of a sale that resold their whole file.
items.fix: Have the verifier record `rows_shared_with_parents` (address-set intersection with each parent body it holds) in the attestation and populate `derivation.added_rows`; render '2,992 of 2,992 rows are identical to pixel-parent-c' on the page and in `patch get`; refuse to list a child ≥95 % identical to a parent unless it declares `derivation.kind: 'update'`.
items.fixed_note: The verifier measures how many of a body's rows are byte-identical to each parent it holds, records it as `rows_shared_with_parents` on the attestation, fails a body whose rows are ALL its parent's, and the knowledge page prints 'N of M rows in this file are identical to X'.

items.title: A lesson the network rejects reaches its teacher as two words — 'Failed verification' — with no score and no way to try again
items.surface: /teacher/<address> lesson rows; the lesson page after announce
items.problem: `teacherProfile` puts only `status` on each lesson row (teach.ts:1784) and the teacher page renders 'Failed verification'. The scores do exist one click away on the public knowledge page's Verification tab (PatchPage.tsx:400-416, 'node-b FAIL 1/2'), but no surface names the question that failed (attestations carry scores, not prompts), nothing offers a retrain, and the consent text has just told the teacher the record is permanent.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-08-teacher-rejected-en-1280.png ('Failed verification · 0 · 0 CREDIT'); operator view for the same anchor: `node-b FAIL free_generation=1/2 · node-c FAIL free_generation=1/2 pre_apply=0/2`; teach.ts:1784.
items.user_cost: The teacher's name is attached to a public failure they cannot read or fix, and the only route to a sale is to guess which question failed and start over — spending another day's quota.
items.fix: Put `attestations: [{verifier, passed, score}]` on the teacher's lesson rows and the lesson view, name the failing sample when the verifier can identify it, add a 'Train again with more effort' action that pre-selects that question, and say in one line that the failed record stays public while a new version is listed separately (publisher-side twins: items 155/157).
items.fixed_note: Teacher lesson rows carry every verification result — verifier, score, and the questions the model got wrong with what it answered — plus the lesson id to train again, and one line saying the failed record stays public while a retrain publishes separately.

items.title: A private lesson lives 7 days and nothing renews it when it is used; the only durable outcomes are publishing or a file that needs two 40 GB GPUs
items.problem: `draftTtlDays` is 7 (packages/core/src/config.ts:72) and `sweepExpired` deletes the draft, its files and its tokens (teach.ts:910-920); `expires_at` is set at finish and at reject and never touched again — loading, trying or opening the lesson does not renew it (grep). The sheet is honest about each option ('Not private from the operator', 'link valid for 7 days', 'needs two 40 GB GPUs … no laptop version yet'), but together they mean the free, private path expires while the permanent, monetised one does not.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-31-keep-private-en-1280.png; config.ts:72; teach.ts:910-920, :1093.
items.user_cost: Work is pushed toward publishing by expiry rather than by choice: a creator who is not ready to publish loses the trained file and spends another day's quota to recreate it.
items.fix: Touch `expires_at` whenever the owner loads, tries or opens the lesson; show 'kept until {date} — renews each time you use it' on the card; send a `teach` event 24 h before expiry with a one-click 'keep another 7 days'; say what happens on day 8 in the sheet.
items.fixed_note: The keep-private sheet and the lesson card both print the node's own expires_at as a date, say that opening or trying the lesson moves it, and say what happens after — instead of a constant "7 days" beside a green success message.

items.title: When an AIN payout to a teacher fails for good, the teacher sees 'transfer failed — still owed by 0x…' and has no button, no channel and no way to reach the operator
items.problem: After `maxAttempts` (20) or a restart mid-transfer the row is `failed` (packages/node/src/payouts.ts:100-101, :157) and the teacher page renders `teacher.item.failed` ('transfer failed — still owed by {seller}', teach.ts:270). The retry endpoint is operator-only (api.ts:355), no visitor-callable nudge exists (grep), and nothing badges the operator's console beyond a warn line.
items.evidence: Code at HEAD: payouts.ts:100-118, :152-162; api.ts:355; teach.ts:270, :1800-1806; the AIN payout path exercised in teach-triggered-38-demo-nodec-ain-payouts.json.
items.user_cost: Real money owed to a visitor depends on an operator noticing a warning in an event feed; the visitor's only evidence is a sentence on a page nobody else looks at.
items.fix: Add `POST /api/teach/payouts/:settle_hash/nudge`, signed with the teaching key, that re-queues the row once and writes a `payout` event naming the teacher; badge the operator's Teaching tab ('1 data-provider payout failed · 4.9 AIN'); show the last error and attempt count with an 'Ask the node to retry' button.
items.fixed_note: POST /api/teach/payouts/:id/nudge, signed with the teaching key the money is owed to, re-queues the transfer once per ten minutes and writes an event naming the payee; the teacher's row shows the last error, the attempt count and the button.

items.title: The split a teacher is offered is the node operator's config, take it or leave it — and there is no way to see what another node offers
items.surface: `teach.contributorShare`; PublishSheet split line; /teach policy; Network page
items.problem: `contributorShare: 0.7` is a node config value (packages/core/src/config.ts:71) surfaced to the teacher as a fact in `teach.pub.split`; there is no negotiation, no per-lesson override, and no surface anywhere that compares nodes' terms (the Network table shows endpoint/name/address/roles/ledger/model/bodies/tracks/last seen). A teacher choosing where to teach cannot compare shares, prices, quorum or the creator share (368).
items.evidence: config.ts:71; packages/web/src/i18n/pages/teach.ts:156; NetworkPage.tsx:106-128; `/api/info` exposes `royalty_share` but no page renders it comparatively.
items.user_cost: The person contributing the data has no lever and no market: the only variable they control is whether to publish at all.
items.fix: Expose `shares` and `royalty_share` per node in `/api/nodes` and the Network table, add a 'Terms' line to the teach policy card ('this node keeps 30 % of your sales; the network's creator share is 30 %'), and let the operator offer a per-lesson share the teacher signs alongside the payout address.
items.fixed_note: `/api/nodes` and every node record carry `shares` (teach / royalty / verifier) so a teacher can compare terms across nodes, and `policy.shares` states what this node keeps as well as what it pays.

items.title: On the data provider's own page the lesson's gross 'Revenue' sits three lines above 'Your share'
items.problem: `teacherProfile.lessons` copies `e.revenue` — the sum of sale amounts (catalog.ts:142) — into a column headed `teacher.h.revenue` ('Revenue' / '매출', teach.ts:254), while the earnings table below is headed `teacher.h.amount` ('Your share').
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-14-teacher-page-as-ancestor-ledger-en-1280.png ('Revenue 10 CREDIT' above 'Your share 3 CREDIT').
items.user_cost: The page that exists to show what a teacher earned opens with a number that is not what they earned.
items.fix: Rename the column 'Sales total' and add a 'Your share' column summing that lesson's earnings rows — one word per number, the same word on both tables.
items.fixed_note: The lessons table's money column is renamed Sales total and a Your share column beside it sums that lesson's earnings rows — one word per number on both tables.

flows.name: C. Royalties and payouts
flows.description: The money that is supposed to reach every creator in a chain: the split, the transfer, and the screens that claim it happened.

items.title: One creator spelled two ways is paid once: 3 of 4.5 AIN never leaves the seller, and on a local ledger the rest lands on a string no wallet matches
items.problem: A data provider is stored with the address as typed (`validateContributors` lower-cases only for the duplicate check, catalog.ts:191-201) while the same person as an ancestor author is keyed by their checksum address; `royaltySplit`'s `add()` sums by raw string (catalog.ts:266, 273-296) and `same()` is used only against the seller/author. `payouts.enqueue` then de-duplicates per `(settle_hash, lower(address))` (packages/node/src/store.ts:545-548, payouts.ts:64-76), so the second spelling silently finds the first row and is skipped; on a local ledger `creditBalance` and `/api/me/wallet` compare exactly (`addr === address`, market.ts:676; api.ts:345), so the credit is invisible and unspendable.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-02-buy-chain-x402.txt (one sale's map: `{0x538b…ee43: 1.5, 0x538b…Ee43: 3}`); seller-royalties-anc-04-payout-case-collapse.txt (real Store+Payouts with a fake wallet: 'node-c owed 4.5 AIN … would receive 1.5 AIN'); seller-royalties-anc-03-who-sees-what.txt (owed 26.15, balance +19.15, wallet lists 9.15). Re-verified at HEAD after the §11 pass-2 fix.
items.user_cost: The person who contributed the data is paid a third of what the public record says they are owed, and no screen on either node shows a discrepancy.
items.fix: Normalise at the boundary: lower-case (or EIP-55) `c.address` in `validateContributors` and `entry.anchor.author` inside `add()`; compare case-insensitively in `creditBalance`, `/api/me/wallet` and `teacherProfile`; sum folded keys in `payouts.enqueue` before inserting; fold keys when reading historical settle records. Unit test: a royalty map with one address in two cases produces one payout row with the summed amount.
items.fixed_note: royaltyPlan sums addresses case-insensitively under their first-seen spelling, payouts.enqueue folds the spellings before inserting a row, and creditBalance and /api/me/wallet compare case-insensitively — one person in two spellings is now one payee with the summed amount. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: covered by the named core test and by creditBalance folding case on the live cluster.

items.title: A sale whose lineage does not resolve on the seller's node pays the seller 100 % and no record says why — 3 of 37 demo sales did exactly that
items.problem: The walk skips a parent the seller's map does not hold, with no trace (`const e = all.get(id); if (!e) return;`, catalog.ts:249-252), so the pool is 0 and the whole price goes to the seller; the settle record broadcast to every peer looks like a normal sale. The defensive branch below does the same in the other direction: if the split ever exceeded the price the seller would be paid alone and only its own log would know (market.ts:611-615).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-16-demo-ain-reconciliation.txt (the first three qa-royalty-child sales, 08-31 06:37–07:33, settled `{node-c: 10}`; all 34 later ones `{node-a: 3, node-c: 7}`) — 9 AIN of the ancestor's money, silently; commit 76d106d fixed one trigger (visibility:test anchors), not the silent fall-through.
items.user_cost: An ancestor loses their share whenever the seller's node is briefly out of sync with the parent's anchor, and nothing — not the record, not the wallet, not an event — marks those sales as unresolved.
items.fix: Resolve every id in `anchor.parents` before pricing: if any is missing, either refuse with `503 lineage_unresolved: [ids]` or settle with `royalty_unresolved: {id: amount}` and enqueue those amounts against `parent_authors[i]` (the anchor carries the author). Make the over-distribution branch write an `error` event and a failed payout row instead of rewriting the split, and show both states on the seller's payouts screen.
items.fixed_note: An unresolved parent is paid through `parent_authors[i]`, or held back and written onto the settlement as `royalty_unresolved` with an error event on the seller — never folded into the seller's own line — and an over-distribution is scaled proportionally instead of paying the seller the whole price. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: covered by the named core test (an unresolved ancestor is paid through parent_authors or held back on the record).

items.title: The ancestor's wallet reports the seller's promises as money received: 34 payments and 102 AIN on one screen, 29 payout rows on the seller's, 8 transfers on the chain
items.surface: Account → Wallet → 'Creator revenue share received'; `ainize wallet`; `GET /api/me/wallet`
items.problem: `/api/me/wallet` builds `royalties` from settle records naming this address — `{patch_id, amount, created_at}` and nothing else (api.ts:345). Whether the money moved is knowable only from the SELLER's local `payouts` table (payouts.ts), which the ancestor cannot see, and on AIN the transfer happens later, from the seller's wallet, keyed by a push id with no link to the settlement (314). The product already solves this shape for teachers — `teacherProfile` reports owed/paid/pending per settle with the seller named and says 'recorded by {seller} — this node cannot see that transfer' (teach.ts:1792-1817, TeacherPage.tsx:92-94) — and the wallet does not use it.
items.evidence: Reproduced today on the demo cluster: qa-royalty-child has 37 settles (34 with a 3 AIN line to node-a); node-a's wallet lists 34 royalty rows = 102 AIN; node-c's `/api/me/payouts` has 29 rows, all 'paid'; the chain's `/transfer/<node-c>/<node-a>` path holds 8 entries; `ain_getTransactionByHash` on node-c's stored hashes returns null. packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-16-demo-ain-reconciliation.txt, critic-b-02/03.
items.user_cost: The one number that tells a creator whether sharing pays is a claim written by the party that owes the money, with no paid/pending/unverifiable state — and no screen anywhere can reconcile the three totals.
items.fix: Reuse `teacherProfile`'s logic for `market.address` in `/api/me/wallet` and `ainize wallet`: per row `{patch_id, via: <my ancestor id>, seller, buyer, amount, state}` where state is `credited` (local), `confirmed` (a matching chain transfer from that seller), `reported` (the seller's payout endpoint says paid) or `unconfirmed (N days)`; totals for owed / confirmed / unconfirmed; add a public signed `GET /p2p/payouts/:settle_hash` so the ancestor's node can ask.
items.fixed_note: Every wallet royalty row carries its own state — credited / paid / pending / failed / unconfirmed — asked of the seller's node through the new public GET /p2p/payouts/:hash, with owed / in-balance / transferred / unconfirmed totals on Account and in `ainize wallet`, so a promise can no longer be read as a receipt. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — GET /api/me/wallet separates owed/credited/paid/unconfirmed, names the state per row and reports verification income apart from lineage.

items.title: The training set that makes a knowledge worth 25 AIN is a free download, and the promise that buys it — 'I am building on this' — is never checked
items.problem: L1 publishes the questions and answers a knowledge was trained from as a served blob with an access level (packages/node/src/market.ts:550-580, api.ts:223-245). `deriveIntent` costs nothing: any teaching key gets a 24-hour token for the full set, the only side effect is a `derive_fetches` counter (market.ts:574-581), and nothing later checks that the child declared the parent or paid anything; verifiers are exempt unconditionally (market.ts:558-563). The default when a publisher says nothing is `derivative` (teach.ts:2066) — and the publish sheet has no access control and no sentence about it: it sends name/description/price/license/payout/consent only (packages/web/src/components/chat/PublishSheet.tsx:61-70).
items.evidence: Code at HEAD: market.ts:550-581, teach.ts:2066, api.ts:223-245, PublishSheet.tsx:61-70, docs/lineage-teach-design.md §6.1/§6.4.
items.user_cost: The paid asset is the rows; the rows are free to anyone who says the right word. A creator who priced their knowledge at 25 AIN has given away the material to retrain it, and was never asked; the honest derivative who declares lineage and pays 30 % competes with the one who took the same file and declared nothing.
items.fix: Tie the derive token to a commitment: record `{parent_id, child_key, at}` as a `derive` record, and require any anchor whose dataset lists that parent to name it in `parents[]`; make `derivative` access mean 'available to a knowledge that declares this parent', not 'available on request'. Put the access level in the publish sheet with one sentence and a default of `private` unless the teacher opts in, and show 'training set: public / derivative / private' on the knowledge page next to the price.
items.fixed_note: A derive intent is now a recorded commitment: `derive_intents` stores which teaching key took which knowledge's questions and when, the response says what was promised, and the parent's owner can read the list. The promise is enforced — a lesson trained on a set that came from a published knowledge is refused at createJob and again at publish unless it names that knowledge as its base — and the publish sheet says what each access level means before the creator chooses. Node/web 473d2bc, CLI render 69c17fa.

items.title: Payout rows exist only in the seller's SQLite and are never rebuilt from the record: five demo settles owe 3 AIN each and no row anywhere knows it
items.surface: `payouts.enqueue` (called once, inline with the sale); `ainize payouts`
items.problem: `enqueue` is called once from `settlePayment` (market.ts:629) and there is no reconcile pass anywhere (grep finds only the OpenAPI description text). A settle written before the payouts table existed, a wiped data dir, or a crash between `ledger.append` and `enqueue` leaves a public debt with no row — so no retry, no 'failed', nothing. `enqueue` is already idempotent per `(settle_hash, address)`.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-16b-nodec-payout-rows.txt (rows 1–29 start at 09-01 00:00:43) against 34 royalty-bearing settles — the five from 08-31 have no row at all.
items.user_cost: 15 AIN owed to the demo's ancestor is unrecoverable by any button in the product; an honest seller cannot pay a debt the product forgot.
items.fix: At start and on a timer, walk this node's own `ain-transfer` settle records and call `enqueue` for each (idempotent), then `processPending`; add `ainize payouts reconcile` and log 'N rows recovered from the record'. Since settles are the shared source of truth, a missing row then becomes impossible rather than merely unlikely.

items.title: Nothing links a settlement to the payout that honoured it: the creator's share is an unreferenced transfer from the seller's wallet, after the fact
items.problem: The buyer pays the seller in full (`payTo` is the node, market.ts:551); the seller writes the settle with the royalty map; a background runner then sends one transfer per address (payouts.ts:93 → `ain.wallet.transfer({to, value, nonce:-1})`, packages/core/src/ain-ledger.ts:253-257) with no memo and no key tying it to the settle hash, and no `payout` record is appended to the shared ledger. `recordAccess` is written by the buyer for the purchase only (market.ts:815).
items.evidence: seller-royalties-anc-16-demo-ain-reconciliation.txt (34 reported / 29 seller-claimed / 8 in chain state, unreconcilable by anyone); code at HEAD payouts.ts:93, ain-ledger.ts:253-257.
items.user_cost: The landing page's promise — 'payments and creator revenue share settle on the AI Network automatically' — is true for the purchase and unverifiable for the share. A creator has no evidence to dispute a seller, and an honest seller has no evidence to show.
items.fix: Use the settle hash as the transfer key (`/transfer/<seller>/<to>/<settleHash>`; ain-js accepts an explicit key — `transferKeyFor` already exists in packages/core/src/x402.ts:51 and is unused) and append a `payout {settle_hash, to, amount, tx_hash}` record so any node can join settle ↔ payout; show 'confirmed on chain' vs 'seller-reported' in the wallet (311). Longer term let the 402 carry several `payTo` lines so the buyer pays each recipient directly.

items.title: Creator payouts have no home except a tab about taught lessons, and its local-ledger notice describes something the code never does
items.surface: My knowledge → Teaching → Payouts; `ainize payouts ls`
items.problem: The only payouts screen is TeachingTab.tsx:310-345, headed 'Data-provider shares this node owes from sales of taught lessons' (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/operator.ts:558) — yet the same table is where lineage royalties to other nodes appear. Its local-ledger alert says payouts 'are only recorded here and stay pending until it runs on the AI Network' (operator.ts:571), while `settlePayment` enqueues only for `ain-transfer` (market.ts:625-631): on a local ledger nothing is recorded at all.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-07-payouts-under-teaching-en-1280.png ('No payouts yet — they appear when a taught lesson sells · Owed 0' after three sales owing 12.3 CREDIT to two other nodes); seller-royalties-anc-03-who-sees-what.txt (`payouts ls` → '(none)').
items.user_cost: A seller with no teaching activity has no idea the node owes other creators anything, and an operator on a local ledger is told money is pending that was in fact credited instantly.
items.fix: Move Payouts to Account → Wallet under 'What this node owes creators and data providers', with a 'why' column ('creator of p-mid' / 'data provider of p-mid'), and keep a filtered copy in Teaching. On a local ledger, derive the same rows from settle records and say 'credited the moment the sale was recorded — nothing to send'.
items.fixed_note: Account → Wallet gained "What this node owes creators and data providers", folded per payee/knowledge/state with a why column read off the sold anchor (verifier, data provider, or upstream creator); on a local ledger the rows are derived from the settle records and say "credited with the sale", and the Teaching tab’s local-ledger alert no longer claims a transfer is pending.

items.title: The reconciled per-sale earnings view the ancestor needs already exists — at /teacher/<address>, labelled 'Data provider', unlinked from the wallet, counting their own sales and reading only the first spelling of their address
items.problem: `teacherProfile` (teach.ts:1777-1816) walks every settle, matches the address case-insensitively and reports owed/paid/pending/failed with the seller per row — exactly the ancestor's question, for any address, lineage royalties included. But it is reachable only from teach flows, its heading and footer describe a visitor, it counts sales where the viewer is the seller as earnings, `find()` takes only the first matching key (teach.ts:1795 — so the two-spelling case of 309 is undercounted), and 'paid' is known only from the payouts table of the node being viewed.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-14-teacher-page-as-ancestor-ledger-en-1280.png ('Owed 16.4 · Paid 16.4 · 6 sales' including the viewer's own g-root sale) against the wallet's 19.65 and the ledger's 26.15 — three totals for one person.
items.user_cost: Three surfaces give one creator three answers, and the one closest to right cannot be reached from the wallet.
items.fix: Reuse `teacherProfile.earnings` in `/api/me/wallet` for the node address and any payout address, summing every key that folds to it and excluding rows where the viewer is the seller; render it as the wallet's 'Creator revenue share' table with the per-seller state; link 'see every sale' from the wallet and keep /teacher/ as the public page.

items.title: The wallet's arithmetic does not close: gross sale amounts above a net balance, with no line for what left
items.problem: `/api/me/wallet` returns `settlement.amount` per sale (api.ts:344) and AccountPage renders it unchanged (AccountPage.tsx:149-155) under a blurb that says 'initial credit + revenue received − purchases'. Node B's page lists sales of 3, 3, 98, 3 (107) with a balance of 175.5 = 100 + 75.5; the missing 31.5 went to node-a as the creator share and no row says so. (Item 194 covers the gross `revenue` stat on the dashboard and `patch get`; this is the wallet, where the balance sits next to it.) The per-sale split does exist — on the knowledge's Logs page (LogsPage.tsx:79-83).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-03-who-sees-what.txt (balance 128.35 against sales totalling 40.5); chain-buy-human-20-seller-b-account-notes.json; api.ts:344, AccountPage.tsx:149-155.
items.user_cost: A seller cannot see what declaring a parent costs them per sale, so the first reaction to the split is to distrust the wallet rather than to price the derivative.
items.fix: Return `{amount, mine, shared:[{address, name, amount, role}]}` per sale from `settle.royalty`; render Sales as Amount · Your share · Creator share (to whom) with a totals row and a 'Creator share paid to others: −31.5' line under the balance; print `AMOUNT YOURS SHARED` and `net revenue` in `ainize wallet`.
items.fixed_note: Each sale shows what stayed here beside what was charged, names who the rest went to, totals both, and one line under the balance reconciles them; `ainize wallet` prints YOURS/SHARED and net revenue (5ea0d95).

items.title: A derivative can be listed under its base at any price with no warning and no notice to the ancestor
items.problem: `createDraft` checks only that each parent id is known (market.ts:330-339) and `validatePrice` accepts any non-negative decimal (catalog.ts:170-173). The form's helper says 'Their creators automatically get a share of every sale' — no parent price, no net figure, no floor. Because today's children carry the parent's rows, a 0.5-credit child is the 10-credit parent plus extras; the parent's author gets no event (`noticeOwnEvents` covers challenge/supersede/fail on their own anchors only, market.ts:250-275).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-01-publish-chain.txt (u-cheap at 0.5 under a 10-credit parent, LISTED) and -02 (its sale paid the grandparent 0.15); seller-royalties-anc-09-new-patch-form-en-1280.png.
items.user_cost: The parent's price is undercut by its own child and their per-sale take drops from 10 to 0.15, discovered only if they happen to open their own knowledge's lineage list. Nothing makes sharing a base safer than hoarding it.
items.fix: At draft and publish show the parents' prices and the computed net ('parent g-root sells at 10; at 0.5 you keep 0.35 and g-root's creator gets 0.15') and warn when the price is below the base's; let an anchor carry an optional `derivative_floor` verifiers enforce on children; emit a `derived` event on the parent author's node when a child naming their knowledge is ingested, and list children with their prices on the ancestor's manage page.
items.fixed_note: The publish path prints every parent's price and the computed split before the announce, and warns when the listing is cheaper than a base whose rows it carries ("1 CREDIT is below h-root2's own price of 4 — its creator's take drops from 4 to a royalty slice"). The notice half landed in bef7ed5: the ancestor's node logs a `lineage` warning naming the child, its author and its price the moment the anchor arrives, and the manage page lists children with price, author, sales and what they have paid. No `derivative_floor` was added — a floor a verifier enforces would need a network rule change, and the finding's own user cost is answered by telling both sides.

items.title: The ancestor is never told they earned anything, and the 'Notifications: sales only' setting is stored and read by nothing
items.surface: Ledger ingest; operator event feed; Account → Notifications
items.problem: A settle naming this node as an ancestor arrives through gossip and is logged as 'received 1 record(s) via push' (api.ts:878); `noticeOwnEvents` skips every entry whose author is not this node (market.ts:253), so no `royalty` or `derived` event is ever emitted for the recipient. `notifications` appears only in the settings schema (api.ts:462), the getter/setter (market.ts:1102-1110) and the Account form (AccountPage.tsx:22-59) — no reader anywhere. (Item 195 covers the missing attribution on the wallet row; the dead setting and the missing ingest event are new.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-03-who-sees-what.txt (node-c's events after four royalty-bearing settles: only p2p push lines); grep for `notifications` across packages/node/src and packages/web/src.
items.user_cost: The signal that should make a creator publish more — 'someone built on this and it paid' — never fires, and the setting that promises it is decorative.
items.fix: On ingest of a settle where `royalty[me] > 0` (case-insensitive) emit `info royalty 'earned 3 CREDIT from c-leaf (sold by node-a)'`; on ingest of an anchor naming my knowledge as a parent emit `info derived`; filter the feed by the notifications setting and badge My knowledge — or remove the setting until it does something.
items.fixed_note: A settle whose royalty map names this node emits an `info royalty` event with the amount, the child, the seller and the ancestor it was earned through. The `notifications` setting is read at last: `all` = every derived notice, `sales` = money and anything that stops money (challenge, FAIL, supersede, byte copy), `none` = nothing — and a suppressed notice is never marked seen, so turning it back on delivers it. Verified live: with `sales`, a new child produced no notice; switching to `all` delivered it.

items.title: A creator's earnings cannot leave the node: there is no send, no withdraw, and `chain fund` works only on a local dev chain
items.problem: The CLI's money verbs are `wallet` (read-only), `payouts ls/retry` (outgoing royalties only) and `chain fund <address>` — which `chainFund` refuses unless the provider is local (packages/cli/src/commands/chain.ts:103-112). There is no `wallet send`, no withdraw, no export of the key to a wallet app beyond `keys backup`, and the Account page shows a balance with no action. A node that has earned AIN can spend it only by buying other knowledge through the same node.
items.evidence: packages/cli/src/bin.ts:397-404 (the whole money surface); chain.ts:103-112; AccountPage.tsx:133-135 (balance, no action).
items.user_cost: 'You get paid per sale' ends at a number on one screen: a creator cannot move earnings to their own wallet, pay a collaborator, or take anything off the node — which also makes the play-money problem (299) indistinguishable from the real one.
items.fix: Add `ainize wallet send <address> <amount>` (AIN ledgers) with a confirm and a tx hash, and an Account action beside the balance; on local ledgers say plainly that the balance cannot leave this node and link the terms.

items.title: The one payout the code refuses to retry automatically reaches the operator as a sentence cut off before the instruction
items.problem: `payoutTable` truncates `last_error` to 48 characters (packages/cli/src/commands/branch.ts:76) and `PAYOUT_INTERRUPTED` is 93 ('node restarted during the transfer — confirm on chain whether it went through before retrying', payouts.ts:32) — the half that is removed is the instruction. `recoverInterrupted` sets `attempts = maxAttempts` so the row reads 'failed (gave up)' and `due()` never picks it up; `ainize status` has no payouts line.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-15-cli-interrupted-payout-render.txt (the rendered row against the full 93-character message); branch.ts:71-77; payouts.ts:32, :152-162.
items.user_cost: The operator either retries blind — risking the double payment the code was written to prevent — or never notices, and the creator on the other node stays unpaid.
items.fix: Never slice `last_error`: print it on its own indented line and, for `PAYOUT_INTERRUPTED`, append the concrete command ('check /transfer/<seller>/<to> on the chain, then `ainize payouts retry N`'). Add 'payouts needing attention: N' to `ainize status` and a banner on My knowledge when `summary.failed > 0`.

items.title: Naming two parents costs exactly what naming one costs, and the rule that decides it lives in a source comment
items.problem: The pool is split equally between unique ancestor AUTHORS at any depth, each author's slice is divided among their anchors, and their data providers carve from that slice (catalog.ts:266-296) — so a merge naming p-mid and g-root paid exactly what a plain child naming p-mid alone paid, and a grandparent out-earned the direct parent because the parent had declared a data provider. Nothing user-facing states the rule: `ainize publish` prints no split (item 189) and the form helper says only 'Their creators automatically get a share'. (Item 192 reports the undisclosed inheritance and depth cut; the equal-per-author rule and the free merge are new.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-02-buy-chain-x402.txt (m-merge and c-leaf royalty maps identical); seller-royalties-anc-01-publish-chain.txt; catalog.ts:266-296; docs/lineage-teach-design.md §11.
items.user_cost: A creator deciding whether to build on one base or combine two, or whether declaring a data provider is affordable, makes a permanent revenue decision with no number in front of them.
items.fix: Add `GET /api/patches/:id/split` (and `ainize publish --preview`) returning `royaltySplit` for the draft's parents, contributors and price as `[{address, name, role, amount}]`, render it as 'Who gets what per sale' on the form and before the CLI confirm, and state the rule in one sentence in the helper and /docs.

items.title: 'royalties received 1' is a count printed where every other line is an amount, and 'Revenue shared with 0xbb98F284…' names neither the person nor the share
items.surface: `ainize wallet`; Knowledge page → Origins 'Revenue shared with'
items.problem: `branch.ts:90-91` prints `['sales', x.sales.length]` and `['royalties received', x.royalties.length]` directly under `balance 100.9 CREDIT`; PatchPage.tsx:455 renders `parent_authors` as short addresses with no name lookup (the same page names the node two lines above) and no share, under a sentence that quotes the viewing node's rate.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-06-cli-buy-child.txt (node-a: 'royalties received 1' above a table whose only amount is 0.9); chain-buy-human-07-child-visitor-notes.json.
items.user_cost: The ancestor misreads what they earned (1 vs 0.9) and a buyer cannot tell who profits from the family they are about to pay into.
items.fix: Print `sales 1 (3 CREDIT)` and `royalties received 0.9 CREDIT (1 payment)`; in Origins render 'node-a (0xbb98…3196) · receives 30 % of each sale' using the tree's own name lookup, and list the whole payee set from `royaltySplit` rather than the direct parents (item 193).
items.fixed_note: `ainize wallet` prints sales and royalties as amounts over counts, and the Origins block names every payee with the share and amount (5ef4eb4).

items.title: Declared data providers vanish after publishing: `patch get` never prints them and the knowledge page renders only the first of four
items.problem: The publish confirmation lists them ('data providers on the record: dave 50 %', packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:168) but the detail renderer has branches for attestations, lineage, conflicts, branches and settlements and none for `anchor.contributors` (patch.ts:47-110). `PatchPage.tsx:153` picks `contributors?.find(c => c.role === 'data_provider')` — the first only, though an anchor may carry four (`MAX_CONTRIBUTORS`, types.ts:84). (Item 198 covers the missing CLI line; the dropped second, third and fourth provider on the web page is new.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/seller-royalties-anc-01-publish-chain.txt against seller-royalties-anc-03-who-sees-what.txt (`patch get p-mid` with no contributor line); PatchPage.tsx:153.
items.user_cost: A seller checking what its record promises cannot see who will be paid from its share, and a second data provider is invisible to every buyer.
items.fix: Add a 'data providers' block to `patch get` (name, share of the seller's remainder, proof) and render all contributors with their effective share on the knowledge page.
items.fixed_note: Every credited data provider is named in the header (not just the first of four) and each is paid a named, measured share in the money block; the `patch get` block is item 198, in the CLI workstream.

flows.name: D. Verification economics
flows.description: What it costs to be a verifier, what it returns, and what the badge a buyer pays for is actually worth.

items.title: Verifying is unpaid work: 501 attestations and 2,765 AIN of sales on the demo chain, and not one credit has ever reached a verifier
items.problem: `royaltySplit` distributes a sale between the seller, ancestor authors and contributors only (packages/core/src/catalog.ts:236-306); there is no `verifierShare` anywhere in packages/core or packages/node (grep), and `/api/me/wallet` has sales, royalties, purchases and payouts — no place a verification could appear. Meanwhile the landing page and glossary invite operators to 'take part in verification' (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/public.ts:48, glossary.ts:41) with no word about cost or return. (Item 127 is about the deposit that is never escrowed; this is compensation, which has never existed.)
items.evidence: Recounted from node-b today: 501 attestations (node-b 209, node-c 203), 462 settlements, 2,765.8 AIN of volume, 0 royalty lines naming node-b; packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-nodeb-demo-worktime.txt (184 benchmark runs = 54.9 min of exclusive model lock); verifier-economy-demo-nodeb-account-en-1280.png ('0 sale(s) · 0 creator-share payment(s) received' after 203 verifications).
items.user_cost: The role every default node takes (config.ts:188) costs a GPU, ~1 GB of other people's bodies and minutes of model lock per item, and earns nothing. A rational operator turns it off, and the quorum every listing needs disappears with it; the economy has a producer, a buyer, an ancestor, and a fourth party that only pays.
items.fix: Add `market.verifierShare` (default 0.05–0.1) and a third pass in `royaltySplit(entry, all, amount, share, verifierShare, executed)`: carve it from the seller remainder and split it equally among the addresses of the attestations that currently count for that entry (`deriveCatalog` already computes `executed`, catalog.ts:136). They then land in `settle.royalty`, so `payouts` pays them on AIN and `creditBalance` credits them locally with no new code. Surface it: `verification: [...]` in `/api/me/wallet`, an 'earned from verifying' line in `ainize wallet` and on Account, and the rate on /docs and the verification tab. docs/p2p-compute-market-design.md §7.5 already designs the fee and its strikes — this is that design's first half.
items.fixed_note: The attestations that count for an entry are paid `verifier_share` (0.05 network floor) of the seller side of every sale: verified live on a throwaway cluster, where a 10-CREDIT sale settled {verifier 0.25, verifier 0.25, seller 9.5} and a lineage sale settled {parent author 3.175, verifier 0.175, seller 6.65}; the wallet, `ainize wallet` and the family-tree money card print what verifying earns. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live on the local cluster AND on the AIN dev chain — every settlement’s royalty map names the two verifiers at 0.1 of a 4 CREDIT sale beside the seller’s 3.8.

items.title: Anyone who says they are a verifier downloads every knowledge body for free — the claim is an unsigned POST, and 91 of 132 node records on the demo chain already make it
items.problem: `mayDownload` exempts any address that carries the `verifier` role either in the chain's self-written node registry (write rule `auth.addr === $addr`, packages/core/src/ain-ledger.ts:318) or in the local peer table (market.ts:645-656) — and the peer table is filled by `POST /p2p/hello`, which takes `endpoint`, `address` and `roles` from an unsigned JSON body (api.ts:861-865). The blob route then honours a signed header from that address. No attestation is required before or after, the exemption never expires, and the 402 text advertises it: 'payment required … (verifiers and authors are exempt)'.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-freerider.txt + .mjs (throwaway key 0x313ec2… → `POST /p2p/hello` 200 → `GET /p2p/blob/<sha>` 200, 3,854,446 bytes for a 5-CREDIT body; control without the hello → 402); verifier-economy-chain-nodes.txt ('nodes on chain 132, claiming verifier 91, distinct endpoints 59'); incentives-network-ns-06 (a never-attesting identity fetching a LISTED 20-credit body).
items.user_cost: Every seller's paid inventory is downloadable for the cost of one HTTP POST, with no record on any ledger. Honest verifiers are the disguise.
items.fix: Sign the hello (require `x-ngram-auth` for purpose `hello:<endpoint>` and use the recovered address, not the body's), and replace the blanket role exemption with a verification lease: a verifier may fetch a body only while the entry is ANNOUNCED/VERIFYING/CHALLENGED and only until it has written a counted attestation for that sha — one fetch per verifier per anchor, logged as an event on the seller. Drop the exemption from the 402 text.
items.fixed_note: POST /p2p/hello records an address and its roles only when the caller signs `hello:<endpoint>`, and the blanket verifier exemption became a verification lease — the entry must be waiting for that verifier, the lease ends when its attestation lands, at most three fetches, each logged on the seller. Verified live: a throwaway key claiming the role gets 402 instead of the body, and its claim is not recorded. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — an unsigned POST /p2p/hello claiming the verifier role is recorded as an endpoint with address null, and GET /p2p/blob/:sha answers 402.

items.title: Possession is licence: apply, live-test, chat and subscribe check only that the file is on disk, so a verifier runs a seller's whole catalogue for free
items.problem: `applyPatch` requires `blobs.get(sha)` and a live runtime — no purchase, settlement or authorship test (market.ts:826-838, whose own error says 'buy it first'); `testablePatches` filters on `blobs.has` (market.ts:1034-1038); `subscribe` calls `buy()` only `if (!this.blobs.has(sha))` (market.ts:1108-1112). Verification leaves the body in the store permanently (verifier.ts:95), so every item a verifier ever scored is one `apply` away from production use, free — and a whole track can be subscribed to for nothing. (Item 259 reports the subscribe consequence; the root and the apply/chat surfaces are new.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-apply-without-buy.txt (node-b, purchases 0, `patch apply ux4-pixel` → '✓ applied … 끼움: 2992행', `/api/runtime` shows it applied); chain-buy-human-09-verifier-free-copy.txt (node C applies pixel-parent with `purchased:false` and no settle record); chain-buy-agent-14-subscribe-track-grows.txt (node-b subscribes to a track containing a knowledge it verified: purchases 0, balance unchanged).
items.user_cost: The seller's catalogue is deployed and served by peers who never paid, and the seller cannot see who holds it. The only participants who pay are those who do not run a node.
items.fix: Separate possession from licence: a `licenses` table (`patch_id`, source: purchase | author | verification) written by `putPurchase`, `announce` and the verifier; `applyPatch`, `testablePatches`, `chat` and `subscribe` require `hasLicense(patch_id)`, with verification-sourced copies usable only inside `runtime.verify`. Keep the message that already exists ('buy it first') but make it true, and show sellers 'held by N verifier nodes (verify-only)' on Manage.
items.fixed_note: A `licenses` row records where the right to use a body came from, and a ’verification’ row is possession only — refused at apply, in the chat picker, in chat and in subscribe. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK found the fifth door still open: Teacher.contextTargets decided on blob presence alone, so on a verifier node `teach train --patch <someone-else’s>` loaded a verification copy, trained on top of it and would have published a lesson naming an unbought base. Reproduced live and closed in 6955ba1 (`knowledge_not_licensed`, GET /api/teach/bases/:id gains the matching reason, CLI + browser copy in EN+KO).

items.title: A challenge costs nothing, needs no reason, has no limit, and takes a rival off sale for as long as you keep filing them
items.problem: `Market.challenge` appends and broadcasts with no rate limit, no cost, no minimum reason and no requirement that the challenger has ever verified or bought anything (market.ts:471-479); the API defaults the reason to 'manual challenge' (api.ts:338). `deriveCatalog` sets CHALLENGED and `sellable:false` immediately (catalog.ts:147-165) and the gateway answers 423, so every sale stops until some other node spends GPU minutes re-running the benchmark — and the challenger may file again the moment it re-lists. The terms present the challenge as the safeguard that replaced the deposit (public.ts:181).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-challenge.txt (challenge at 11:54:50 → 423 within a second; challenger's balance unchanged; 75 s off sale; a second challenge posted with an empty body `{}` accepted as 'manual challenge'); demo chain today: 0 challenges in 1,3xx records.
items.user_cost: Any node can stop any sale at zero cost, indefinitely; verifiers pay the GPU time; buyers see 'Re-verification requested' on a good item — while an honest challenger who is right gets nothing.
items.fix: Make the deterrent procedural: require `reason.length >= 20`, refuse a second challenge by the same address on the same anchor while one is open or within 24 h of a PASS quorum answering it; record the outcome (`upheld` / `dismissed`) and expose per-address counts on `/api/nodes` and the Network page; log a `challenge upheld` event and count it toward the verifier reputation (337); and make the CLI print what a challenge costs others before sending it.
items.fixed_note: A challenge needs a 20-character reason, one address may hold only one open challenge per anchor and cannot re-file for 24 h after a re-run dismissed one, every challenge records upheld/dismissed on the entry, and the CLI prints what a challenge costs other operators before it sends. All three refusals reproduced live. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — a 3-character reason is refused (400), a second challenge while one is open is refused (409), and a real challenge is logged and answered.

items.title: '2/2 independent verifiers' can be two processes on one host sharing one model server, and the record cannot tell the difference
items.problem: Independence is judged only by `verifier !== author` (catalog.ts:133-136). `Attestation` carries `verified_on: 'vllm:<model>'` and no runtime URL, instance or host (packages/core/src/types.ts:140-152), so two verifier processes pointed at one `NGRAM_RUNTIME_API` count as two independent verifications — which is exactly the demo cluster (node-a/b/c all report `http://localhost:8002`). With no stake, the marginal cost of a second identity is a config file. The product's own plan says so: 'one supervisor, one host, one vLLM … presenting them as verified by independent nodes is what the directive forbids' (docs/production-verification-plan.md:21).
items.evidence: All three demo nodes' `/api/info` runtime = http://localhost:8002 (checked today); packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-patch-verification-en-1280.png ('2/2 · independent · independent'); verifier-economy-challenge.txt (one attestation carries no `pre_apply` because the patch was already applied by the other run — `wasApplied`, runtime.ts:382-390).
items.user_cost: The buyer's only trust signal — the thing the 402 gate checks before taking money — costs a fraudulent seller one extra process, and honest verifiers' work is indistinguishable from it.
items.fix: Put an executor fingerprint on every attestation: `executor: {api, model, instance: sha256(api+model+mailbox).slice(0,16)}` from `runtime.status()`; count `passed` per distinct instance in `deriveCatalog`, expose `executors`, and render 'Verified 2/2 (1 executor — both ran on the same model server)'. Refuse to attest when `wasApplied` was true unless the verifier can restore first: a result with no baseline of its own should not count.
items.fixed_note: Every executed attestation carries an executor fingerprint (API origin, served model and the engine's own start time), deriveCatalog counts distinct engines and unknown ones separately, the knowledge page and `patch get` say how many model servers were behind the attestations, and a run on a node that already has the knowledge applied is refused rather than recorded as a verification. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: the counting half is reproduced live — `patch get` prints "2 attestations without an engine fingerprint" and the entry carries executors/executors_unknown. The fingerprint against a real engine stays deferred (no engine available).

items.title: A challenge is answered by one re-run from anyone, and the challenger's own pre-challenge PASS fills the quorum that clears its own challenge
items.problem: `deriveCatalog` holds an entry CHALLENGED only while the challenge is newer than `listed_at`, and `listed_at` is the newest counted attestation (catalog.ts:147-151); `effectiveAttestation` falls back to a verifier's pre-challenge record when it has none after (catalog.ts:51-61). So one new PASS by any node moves the entry past the challenge and the second quorum slot is filled by a stale record — including the challenger's own.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-challenge.txt (node-b challenged 11:54:51; node-c alone re-ran at 11:56:06; the item was LISTED 2/2 with node-b's 11:53:42 row still counted, while node-b's own re-run finished only at 11:56:24).
items.user_cost: A seller cannot tell whether a cleared challenge was investigated or merely raced past, and a buyer sees 'Verified 2/2' where one of the two is an attestation its own author has publicly disputed.
items.fix: While a challenge is open, count only attestations newer than it, and never count the challenger's pre-challenge record; mark the challenge `answered` only when quorum is reached that way; show on the verification tab which attestations answered it.
items.fixed_note: While a challenge is open only attestations written after it count; a challenge is dismissed when the quorum is re-established that way and upheld the moment one of those re-runs fails. `stale_attestations` says how many were set aside and the verification tab marks them 'not counted'.

items.title: On the AIN ledger a re-verification overwrites the verifier's earlier attestation — the 'permanent public record' of what it said before the challenge is gone
items.problem: Attestations are written to `market/attestations/${patch_id}/${verifier}` with `setValue` and a rule that permits overwrite (`auth.addr === $verifier`, packages/core/src/ain-ledger.ts:230, :315, :366), and the loader reads one value per verifier (:155-157). The item-153 fix relies on `effectiveAttestation` choosing among a verifier's SEVERAL records (catalog.ts:51-61) — which exist only on the local ledger.
items.evidence: Code path at HEAD (not exercised on the shared chain, where publishing is forbidden): ain-ledger.ts:155-157, :230, :315, :366 against catalog.ts:51-61.
items.user_cost: The only asset a verifier accumulates — a signed history it can be held to — is silently rewritable by itself: a PASS that was challenged and re-passed leaves no evidence the challenge was ever answered, and a FAIL→PASS flip leaves no trace.
items.fix: Key attestations by `${patch_id}/${verifier}/${created_at}`, read all children in the loader, and add `data === null` to the write rule so a written slot is immutable; render superseded records greyed on the verification tab as 'superseded by the same verifier on <date>'.
items.fixed_note: Attestations are written to a write-once child per measurement (`…/$patch_id/$verifier/$created_at`) under a rule that adds `data === null`; the loader reads both that and the legacy single-value shape.

items.title: Verifiers burn GPU on every announced item including hidden test listings nobody can buy: 209 of 213 anchors on the demo chain
items.problem: `round` iterates `catalogAll()` — deliberately including `visibility:test` anchors (packages/node/src/verifier.ts:44) — and verifies everything ANNOUNCED/VERIFYING/CHALLENGED (:64-65), with no filter on visibility, price, seller reachability or capacity; the only knob is `intervalMs` (config.ts:207).
items.evidence: Demo chain recounted today: 213 anchors, 209 `test` and 4 `public`; node-b holds 209 attestations; packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-nodeb-demo-worktime.txt ('attested-never-sold 190', 184 completed benchmarks, 54.9 min of model lock, max 181 s).
items.user_cost: 92 % of the verifier's unpaid work is spent on items that were never for sale — every e2e run of every other agent costs each verifier a download and a benchmark, and a real network would see the same from any spammer.
items.fix: Add `verifier.includeTest: false` (skip `visibility:test` unless set), `verifier.minPrice` and `verifier.maxPerHour` with a per-round budget, and log one line per round: 'skipped N (test), N (budget)'.
items.fixed_note: `verifier.includeTest` (default false), `minPrice`, `maxPerHour` and `maxModelMinutesPerHour` bound the round, and it logs one line per round naming what it skipped. The demo cluster and the suites that publish test anchors opt back in.

items.title: Verification holds the shared model lock ahead of the node's own paying visitors, and the operator has no cap, priority or schedule
items.problem: `verify` runs inside the exclusive cross-process lock for the whole run — probe, up to 8 baseline completions, apply, up to 40 completions, restore (packages/node/src/runtime.ts:374-377) — and chat requests that wait it out return `503 shared runtime busy` (api.ts:907). `verifier.intervalMs` is the only knob; there is no budget, no quiet hours and no priority for the node's own tickets. (Item 135 reports the invisible lock and item 244 the bake's competition; the priority and budget are new.)
items.evidence: Measured from node-b's events: avg 17.9 s, max 181 s of exclusive lock per item (verifier-economy-nodeb-demo-worktime.txt); all three demo nodes share http://localhost:8002.
items.user_cost: On a node that both serves and verifies — the default — a visitor's live test, the flow that converts, waits behind unpaid work for a stranger.
items.fix: Give verification the lower priority: defer an item when `runtime.queueState().waiting > 0`; add `verifier.maxModelMinutesPerHour` (default 10) and an optional window; show the budget on the verification card (335) so the operator can see why an item waits.
items.fixed_note: The shared-model lock is a priority queue: serving first, this node's own bake next, verification last, ties in arrival order. A round stands aside while anything more urgent is running or queued, and `verifier_work` on /api/info shows the budget and why it is paused.

items.title: Nothing tells a new operator what verifying will cost them — `init` silently makes every node a verifier and no page in the product mentions the bill
items.surface: `ainize init`; /docs; README; the landing operator card
items.problem: `init` defaults roles to seller,verifier,serving and `verifier.auto` to true (packages/core/src/config.ts:188, :207) and prints only 'roles seller, verifier, serving'. /docs has five sections — one-line, CLI, bench.json, REST API, x402 — and none about running a verifier (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/docs.ts:4-30); the landing operator card says 'Run a node to sell knowledge and take part in verification' (public.ts:48).
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-init.txt; node-b on the demo holds 932 MB of other people's bodies after 203 verifications while its dashboard says 'No knowledge yet'.
items.user_cost: The operator discovers the cost after the fact — a gigabyte of strangers' files, minutes of model lock while their own visitors wait, and nothing in the wallet.
items.fix: In `init`, when the verifier role is on, print three lines: what it fetches, what it locks, what it earns (`verifierShare` or 'nothing today'), and how to turn it off. Add a '/docs: running a verifier' section fed by `/api/info` (quorum, share) and put the same sentence on the landing operator card.
items.fixed_note: New how-to "What verifying costs": the disk (measured 351,683,460 bytes in 2 files on a node that published and bought nothing), the shared runtime lock, the 5 % verifier share (measured 0.15 CREDIT over 3 sales) and the two switches that turn it off. The `ainize init` print and the landing operator card are CLI and landing work.

items.title: The operator console shows verification as no work at all: 203 attestations and the dashboard says 'No knowledge yet'
items.problem: `DashboardPage.tsx` renders own knowledge, purchases and tracks only (no `attest` anywhere in the file); Account shows 'Roles: verifier' and the quorum rule; `ainize status` prints `blobs held N` with no attestation count, model time, disk figure or outcome. The only record is one log line per start and one per benchmark, without durations.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-demo-nodeb-dashboard-en-1280.png ('No knowledge yet — register your first one' on a node with 203 attestations); verifier-economy-nodeb-console.txt.
items.user_cost: The operator cannot answer 'what did my node do this week, what did it cost, what came back' — the three questions that decide whether the role stays on. Nor can they see that 0 of 501 attestations on the whole network was a FAIL.
items.fix: Add `GET /api/me/verification` → `{attested, passed, failed, hash_only, model_seconds, disk_bytes, sold_after_verification, earned}` from `ledger.attestations()`, the `verifying → benchmark` event pairs and `blobs.list()`; render it as a card at the top of the dashboard for nodes with the role and a line in `ainize status`.
items.fixed_note: A verification block on the dashboard counts what this node signed — attested, passed, failed, integrity-only, knowledges, earned — plus the network-wide failure count, all from signed records; the `ainize status` line is left to the node workstream.

items.title: Verified bodies are never released: nothing purges them, there is no retention setting, and the seller cannot see who is holding what
items.problem: `ensureBlob` stores every verified body (verifier.ts:95) and the only `blobs.remove` in the product is in `patch forget` (market.ts:628) — no TTL, no `verifier.retainBodies`, no post-attestation cleanup. The manifest knows the holder set (`p2p.holders`, market.ts:747) but no seller-facing surface shows it.
items.evidence: node-b on the demo: 932 MB under data/blobs after 203 verifications, none purchased (verifier-economy-nodeb-demo-worktime.txt); grep for retain/prune/purge in packages/node/src returns nothing. (Item 128 reports that disk use is not shown; the absence of any retention policy, and the seller's blindness, are new.)
items.user_cost: A verifier's disk grows without bound with files it may not use once 327 lands, and a seller can never tell replication from an unpaid copy.
items.fix: After a counted attestation, drop the body unless the node authored or bought it (`verifier.retainBodies`, default false); report bytes held and released in `ainize status` and on the verification card; show sellers 'held by N nodes (verify-only)' from `p2p.holders` on Manage.
items.fixed_note: A verified body is dropped once its attestation is written unless this node authored, bought or serves it; `verifier.retainBodies` keeps the old behaviour and `/api/info.verifier_work` reports files and bytes released.

items.title: Verifiers have no reputation surface: no page, no counts, no fail rate, no challenge history — so a result cannot be weighed and care cannot be rewarded
items.problem: The verification tab prints `verifier_name` and a short address with no link (PatchPage.tsx:405); the Network table has endpoint/name/address/roles/ledger/model/bodies/tracks/last-seen (NetworkPage.tsx:106-128); `/api/nodes` returns PeerInfo. There is a `/teacher/:address` route and no `/verifier/:address` (App.tsx:72). Nothing aggregates attestations, FAILs, challenges raised or attestations later challenged.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-demo-network-en-1280.png (seven throwaway node-d identities on one endpoint, all 'verifier', indistinguishable from a node with 200 attestations).
items.user_cost: A buyer weighs 'node-b · Passed' exactly as heavily as a key created five minutes ago, and a verifier that does careful work cannot be told from one that has never failed anything — so there is no reason to be careful.
items.fix: Add `/verifier/:address` and `GET /api/verifiers/:address` computed from the ledger (attested / passed / failed / hash-only / executors / challenges raised and upheld / attestations later challenged); link the verification tab's verifier cell to it; add Attested and Failed columns to the Network table and `ainize nodes`, and collapse duplicate endpoints into one row.
items.fixed_note: GET /api/verifiers/:address and /verifier/:address compute a verifier's record from signed attest and challenge records — signed, passed, failed, hash-only, counting today, rechecks, later challenged, disagreements, challenges raised and their outcomes, distinct engines and measured work — and the verification tab links to it.

items.title: The safeguard that replaced the deposit has never fired: 501 attestations, 0 FAIL, 0 challenges — and no screen says so
items.surface: Verification tab note; /terms 2.3; README 'What Verified is and is not'
items.problem: After item 127 the product honestly says nothing is escrowed and points to challenges as the check (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/detail.ts:165, public.ts:181, README.md:131). Because a challenge pays nothing (328) and a wrong PASS costs nothing (325, 337), the mechanism has no reason to fire — and no surface shows the base rate that would let a reader judge a 100 % pass rate.
items.evidence: Demo chain recounted today: 501 attestations, FAIL 0, challenges 0; docs/production-verification-plan.md:21 says the same; `/api/info` has no verification statistics (api.ts:142).
items.user_cost: A buyer reads 'any node can challenge a wrong one' and infers oversight that has never happened once; trust is borrowed from a mechanism with zero observed activity.
items.fix: Render the base rate next to the claim from a new `/api/info.verification_stats`: 'On this network: 501 verifications, 0 failed, 0 challenges (0 upheld)' — computed once per catalogue derivation. Keep the sentence; attach the number.
items.fixed_note: /api/info.verification_stats counts attestations, failures, challenges and upheld challenges across the record, and the knowledge page prints the base rate under the 'any node can challenge it' sentence — saying so in words when it is 0 and 0.

items.title: To re-check an item honestly, a verifier is told to challenge it first — the refusal steers careful work into taking a seller off sale
items.surface: `ainize patch verify <id>` on an item this node already attested
items.problem: `verifyOne` refuses a second run with 'a second attestation would not be counted. Re-verification counts after someone challenges the knowledge (ainize patch challenge …)' (verifier.ts:85-91) — the only exception being a hash-only upgrade. There is no way to record a fresh measurement after a model update or a buyer complaint without stopping the seller's sales.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-verify-again.txt (the exact refusal text).
items.user_cost: A verifier with a doubt can stay silent or attack; most operators will stay silent, which is the opposite of what the trust story needs.
items.fix: Add `ainize patch verify <id> --recheck`: run the benchmark and write an attestation flagged `recheck`; let `effectiveAttestation` prefer a newer FAIL recheck from the same verifier (so a PASS can be withdrawn without a challenge) and leave a PASS recheck as a visible confirmation. Name that option first in the refusal.
items.fixed_note: `ainize patch verify <id> --recheck` (and POST .../verify {"recheck": true}) records a fresh measurement without stopping the sale; a failing recheck withdraws the verifier's earlier PASS in deriveCatalog, and the refusal names the option first.

items.title: The attestation records no measure of the work: no duration, no samples run, no executor — so verification can never be priced, audited or compared
items.problem: The record carries score, passed, verified_on, restarts and collateral. `runtime.verify` caps a run at 40 samples (runtime.ts:377) and keeps per-call timings in a `log` array that is never persisted (verifier.ts:126-131), so a 4-question run and a 40-question run on a 2,761-fact item look identical to every reader and to any future payout rule.
items.evidence: types.ts:140-152; runtime.ts:374-424; a demo attestation body: `{free_generation: '4/4', pre_apply: '0/4'}`.
items.user_cost: Any incentive built on top (325) has to be flat per attestation, which rewards the cheapest possible run; buyers cannot see that one '4/4' cost 3 s and another '40/40' cost three minutes.
items.fix: Add `duration_ms`, `samples_run`, `samples_available` and `executor` (329) to the attestation body, include them in the signed message, and render 'samples_run/available · duration' on the verification tab and in `patch get`.
items.fixed_note: `duration_ms`, `samples_run` and `samples_available` are on the signed attestation body; the verification tab, the verifier page and `patch verify` all print questions-run-of-available and seconds.

items.title: On a gas-charging chain every attestation is a write the verifier signs and pays for, and nothing budgets, reimburses or stops it
items.problem: Attestations are written under the verifier's own transaction (ain-ledger.ts:366, rule `auth.addr === $verifier`), so any gas is debited from the verifier; today it is zero only because the dev chain runs `ENABLE_GAS_FEE_WORKAROUND` (deploy/docker-compose.ain.yml:21). The product's own plan assigns 'seller pays gas on anchor/attest/settle/payout' (docs/production-verification-plan.md:267), which cannot hold for a record the verifier signs, and estimates ~0.19 AIN of gas around a 0.1 AIN purchase (§5.8). `verifier.auto` keeps attesting until the balance runs out, with no minimum-balance guard.
items.evidence: ain-ledger.ts:315, :366; docker-compose.ain.yml:21-22; production-verification-plan.md:264-267. Prospective: no gas is charged today.
items.user_cost: The moment the product moves to a signature-verifying, gas-charging chain, the unpaid role becomes a net-paying role, and the node will keep writing until it is broke.
items.fix: Decide it with `verifierShare` (325): record `gas_paid` on the attestation, floor the verifier's line at its gas, stop `round()` with a warn below `verifier.minBalance`, and correct the plan's gas-payer line.
items.fixed_note: verifier.minBalance (default 1, ignored on the local ledger, which has no gas) stops the round below the floor with one warn naming the balance, the floor and how to fund it, and one info on recovery; the balance is read at most once a minute and an unanswering chain is not read as an empty account. docs/production-verification-plan.md now says the verifier pays gas on its own attestation. No gas is charged today, so the guard could not be exercised end to end.

items.title: The publish sheet tells a data provider the node 'keeps the rest for training, hosting and verification' — verification is done by other nodes and this sale pays them nothing
items.problem: packages/web/src/i18n/pages/teach.ts:156 (en and ko) justifies the node's cut with a cost the node does not bear: `royaltySplit` has no verifier payee (catalog.ts:236-306) and verification runs on other peers' GPUs.
