items.evidence: teach.ts:156; the settle records of every taught lesson in packages/e2e/results/ux4/teach-triggered-14/23 (seller, contributor and ancestors only).
items.user_cost: A teacher negotiating their share believes part of the node's cut funds the verification that makes their lesson sellable; it does not, and the peers who do it are unpaid.
items.fix: Reword to what the split does — 'keeps the rest for training and hosting. Verification is done by other nodes, which receive {verifierShare}% of each sale / and is not paid from this sale' — driven from `/api/info` so it follows 325 automatically.
items.fixed_note: The verification sentence is driven from policy.shares.verifier (0.05 on a default node): where verifiers are paid it says what they receive and that it comes out of the node's share, and where they are not it says this sale pays them nothing. "training, hosting and verification" is gone from the node's justification.

items.title: A verifier that buys what it already holds is told 'body already present' and never learns what the payment bought
items.surface: `ainize patch buy` on a held body
items.problem: `market.buy` prints `download  body already present; sha256 matches on-ledger anchor` (market.ts:696) with no sentence about what the money did buy — a settlement, a licence and (on AIN) an access receipt.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/critic-03-nodeb-rebuy-pixelplus.txt and verifier-economy-demo-buy.txt (node-b, a verifier, paid 0.1 AIN → 'body already present').
items.user_cost: 0.1–25 AIN spent with a message that reads as 'nothing happened' — the operators who notice will stop buying and use the held body, which is exactly the free-riding of 327.
items.fix: When the blob is held and no purchase row exists, print 'body already held by this node (fetched for verification); this purchase records your licence: settlement <hash>' and mark the dashboard row 'Licensed (file was already held as a verifier)'.
items.fixed_note: A verifier buying what it already holds is told before the money moves that the file is here because this node verified it and that buying records the licence, and afterwards — beside the node's own 'body already present' step — what the payment bought: 'the file was already on this node (fetched to verify it) — what 0.1 AIN bought is the licence: settlement <hash>, and <id> may now be used, taught on and subscribed with here'. Verified live on a verifier node for the `patch get` half; the purchase itself needs a sellable knowledge (deferred).

flows.name: E. Trust and finality
flows.description: Who can collect a paid file, what a receipt proves, and how a buyer judges a peer they have never met.

items.title: An AIN payment is a bearer ticket: whoever presents the tx hash first collects the file, and the real payer is told 'payment already used'
items.problem: The ain branch of `settlePayment` verifies only that the transfer executed, went to the seller and was large enough (market.ts:704-712). It ignores the nonce and the resource the 402 issued, never checks `from` against the requester, needs no signature, and `transfer_key` — declared on `X402Requirement` and computable by `transferKeyFor` (packages/core/src/x402.ts:51) — is never set (`AinLedger.transfer` drops the key, ain-ledger.ts:253-257). The manifest is issued to `settlement.buyer` but returned to whoever made the HTTP request, and its 24-hour token is checked by token+sha alone (store.ts:334-337). Every transfer on an AIN chain is public.
items.evidence: Reproduced live today with 0.1 AIN (critic-04-ain-bearer-token.txt): node-b transferred and did not redeem; a request carrying node-b's tx hash with `x-ngram-buyer` set to node-c and no signature got HTTP 200, a manifest `issued_to` node-b, and 3,854,446 bytes with the returned token; node-b's own redemption then got 402 'payment already used'. Also packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-02-replay-theft-wrongamount.txt §E3.
items.user_cost: The buyer loses the price and gets nothing; the ledger records them as the buyer of a file someone else took. 'Pay and you get it' — the whole point of x402 — is broken for every AIN sale, and a watcher of `/transfer/*` can front-run all of them.
items.fix: Bind the payment to the quote: put `transfer_key: transferKeyFor(resource, nonce)` in the requirement, have the client transfer with that key, and require `tr.key === transferKeyFor(resource, payload.nonce)` plus `takeNonce(payload.nonce)` in `settlePayment`; require a signature over `sha256(txHash+nonce)` by `tr.from` and reject a requester who is not the payer. Bind the download token to the buyer (`checkToken(token, sha, address)`), or drop it and rely on the signed-buyer path `mayDownload` already implements.
items.fixed_note: An AIN payment is bound to the quote it answers: the 402 carries `transfer_key = transferKeyFor(resource, nonce)`, AinLedger.transfer writes at that key instead of a random push id, and settlePayment requires tr.key to match, the nonce to be this node's and unused, and a `proof` over sha256("x402-ain:<tx>:<nonce>") signed by tr.from — so the manifest can only go to the address that paid. Verified live on the dev chain: a transfer with no quote key bought nothing; a watcher presenting the payer's tx hash was refused for want of a proof, and refused again when it signed with its own key; the payer redeemed, and redeemed again idempotently. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live against the AIN dev chain — packages/node/test/ain.test.ts now passes end to end, so a real transfer carrying the quote’s transfer_key and a proof over sha256("x402-ain:<tx>:<nonce>") is what redeems the manifest.

items.title: The manifest's download token is a transferable bearer: one purchase, unlimited redistribution for 24 hours, recorded nowhere
items.problem: `issueManifest` mints a 24-hour token bound to the sha and stores `issued_to` (market.ts:744-753), but `checkToken` looks up token+sha only (store.ts:334-337) and `mayDownload` returns true on a token with no address at all (market.ts:646). The manifest — token included — is the body of the 200 response, so it is trivially shareable, and nothing counts or limits redemptions.
items.evidence: critique4-01/critic-04 helper run (mint.mjs): a party holding only the token fetched the 72,750-byte body with no signature and no address (HTTP 200), while the same URL without the token returned 402.
items.user_cost: A single 25 AIN purchase can serve an unlimited number of downloads for a day, and the seller has no record that it happened — the per-download billing model has no enforcement behind it.
items.fix: Bind the token to the buyer (`issued_to`) and require it alongside a signed `x-ngram-auth` from that address, or drop the token entirely (settled buyers can already fetch with a signed header); count redemptions per token and log them as a seller event.

items.title: A buyer who paid before a challenge is never told the knowledge they are serving is now disputed
items.problem: The notable-event scan skips every entry whose author is not this node (`if (e.anchor.author.toLowerCase() !== this.address.toLowerCase()) continue;`, market.ts:253), so `challenge`, `fail` and `supersede` notices reach the seller only. `/api/me/purchases` rows carry entry and applied state but no `challenged` flag (api.ts:275-278). Item 156 fixed the author's notice; the buyer was not included.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/verifier-economy-challenge.txt (node-c bought at 11:54:25, node-b challenged at 11:54:51, node-c's `ainize logs` shows only its own verifier lines).
items.user_cost: The buyer keeps serving answers a verifier has publicly disputed, with money already spent and no signal anywhere; the terms promise a challenge 'stops the sale' and say nothing about the people who already bought.
items.fix: Extend the scan to entries in `store.listPurchases()`, emitting `warn/challenge` '<who> challenged knowledge you bought (<id>): <reason> — it is loaded in your model'; add `challenged` to `/api/me/purchases` and a red chip in the Purchased table.
items.fixed_note: The notable-event scan now also reads this node's purchases, so a challenge, a failed verification and a supersede reach the buyer once each, saying what they paid and whether it is loaded; /api/me/purchases rows carry `challenged`, `failed_verifications` and `superseded_by`.

items.title: There is no dispute record anywhere: a buyer who received a wrong file has nothing but an unpaid challenge, and nothing on the ledger says a sale was contested
items.problem: /terms is honest — 'refunds are at the seller's discretion and are not mediated by the protocol', 'a payment is an AIN token transfer and is final once executed' (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/public.ts:183) — and there is no dispute or refund route in api.ts (grep). Non-delivery is in fact recoverable (a settled buyer can fetch the body with a signed header, market.ts:651, verified in critic-01) — the unrecoverable case is a file that is wrong or useless, where the only lever is `patch challenge`, which costs the challenger GPU-time-for-others and pays nothing (328), and which no buyer surface offers.
items.evidence: critic-01-recover-blob-signed.txt (delivery is recoverable); public.ts:183; grep for dispute/refund in packages/node/src/api.ts (none); `ainize patch challenge` is a `patch` verb with no buyer entry point in the web.
items.user_cost: The buyer bears all counterparty risk on the one thing they cannot get back — quality — and the network never learns that a sale was contested, so a bad seller's record stays clean.
items.fix: Add a signed `dispute {patch_id, settle_hash, reason}` record any settled buyer may write, shown on the knowledge page and counted per seller on the Network page; offer it from the Purchased table ('This did not work — raise a dispute') and let a dispute (unlike a challenge) not stop sales but require the seller's answer on the record.
items.fixed_note: A signed `dispute` record any settled buyer may write, answered by the seller on the same permanent record; it stops no sale and spends no GPU. GET /api/patches/:id/disputes, `disputeRecordOf` per seller, and a count on every purchase row.

items.title: Nothing on the Network page lets a buyer judge a stranger's node: no sales, no age, no disputes, no delivery record
items.problem: The table shows endpoint, self-declared name, address, roles, ledger, model, bodies, tracks and last-seen (NetworkPage.tsx:106-128) and `/api/nodes` returns PeerInfo (api.ts:256-260) — nothing about trustworthiness. The ledger holds everything needed (settlements as seller, first-seen, attestations, challenges) and none of it is aggregated per node.
items.evidence: Network capture in this round (columns above); api.ts:256-260. Not covered by item 140 (dead rows) or item 201 (creator-side signals).
items.user_cost: Choosing whom to pay in a peer-to-peer market is a trust decision the product supports with two self-asserted fields.
items.fix: Aggregate per node from the ledger — sales completed, first seen, knowledge listed, attestations written, challenges raised/upheld, disputes received — and show it on /network, on `ainize nodes` and beside the seller on the Buy tab.
items.fixed_note: A Track record column counts what each peer's address actually signed: sales, listings, verifications, challenges and how far back its first record goes.

items.title: Node names are self-chosen and unverifiable, and the Buy tab leads with the name
items.problem: `author_name` is written by the seller itself at draft time (`author_name: this.cfg.name`, market.ts:333) and rendered first on the Buy tab with the address in grey behind it (PatchPage.tsx:503); the chain's node record enforces only `auth.addr === $addr` (ain-ledger.ts:318) and the display name is freely editable (`updateSettings`, market.ts:1107-1110).
items.evidence: PatchPage.tsx:503; market.ts:333; the demo Network page lists self-declared names such as 'creator-x' beside seven throwaway identities sharing one endpoint.
items.user_cost: A buyer can be steered to pay an impostor because the trustworthy-looking field is exactly the one a bad actor controls.
items.fix: Lead with the address (or a key-derived identicon) and mark the name 'self-declared'; only elevate a name backed by a verifiable claim (a signed domain, a chain record the buyer can check).
items.fixed_note: The Buy tab's seller row leads with the full address in mono, quotes the display name as the claim it is — "Calls itself \"node-a\" — a name the selling node writes itself, not a verified identity" — and links to the anchor record on the History tab where the registering address can be checked. No identicon: that would be a new visual language for one row.

items.title: 'payment already used' conflates four situations the buyer must act on differently
items.problem: market.ts:699 (local-credit) and :706 (ain) return the identical string from `store.paymentSeen(h)` without looking at who the prior settlement's buyer was — so a double submit, a recovery attempt by the rightful payer, a front-run by someone else (344) and a stale retry are indistinguishable.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-agent-02-replay-theft-wrongamount.txt (the payer's retry after a stranger redeemed); p2p-trust-12-replay-used-payment.txt.
items.user_cost: The buyer cannot choose the right recovery — download, re-pay or dispute — because every failure reads the same.
items.fix: If the prior settlement's buyer is the requester, re-issue the manifest (273); otherwise answer 'this payment was already redeemed by another party' with the settlement hash so the payer can raise a dispute (347).
items.fixed_note: The four cases are now four answers: the payer re-presenting their own payment is re-issued the manifest with no second charge, a stranger replaying someone else’s payment gets `payment already used`, a nonce consumed by an earlier attempt says so and points at a fresh quote, and an expired nonce says `unknown or expired nonce`.

items.title: Every purchase writes the buyer's address into a record broadcast to every peer, and nothing on the Buy tab says so
items.problem: `settlePayment` appends `{patch_id, seller, buyer, amount, scheme, royalty, …}` and broadcasts it (market.ts:718-735); the public Ledger page and `ledger ls` render 'ux4-free · 0 CREDIT · buyer 0x8186…B3E2'. The Buy tab's copy covers price, seller and gateway and never mentions that buying publishes who you are — the terms discuss the record in general terms, and item 237 covers only the subscription record.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/critique4-01-free-is-not-free.txt (`ledger ls --kind settle` shows the buyer's address for a 0-credit item); PatchPage.tsx:494-506.
items.user_cost: A buyer learns only afterwards that their purchases are a public, permanent list — including free ones, where the record buys them nothing.
items.fix: Add one line to the Buy tab and the CLI confirm: 'The sale is recorded publicly: this knowledge, the price and your node address.' Stop writing a settlement for price-0 downloads (277).

items.title: On the AIN path the quote's nonce and expiry are decorative: a 10-minute quote is redeemable forever
items.problem: `requirementsFor` mints a nonce with the amount and `expires_at` (market.ts:655-666) but the ain branch never calls `takeNonce` and never reads the expiry (market.ts:704-712); replay protection rests entirely on `paymentSeen(txHash)`. No money can be lost to a price change, because anchors are immutable (278) — but the binding that would stop the bearer attack (344) is exactly the one that is unused.
items.evidence: Code at HEAD: market.ts:655-666, 704-712; the bearer reproduction in critic-04-ain-bearer-token.txt.
items.user_cost: A quote that says it expires does not, and the field a client is asked to echo has no effect — so a developer cannot tell which parts of the protocol are load-bearing.
items.fix: Consume the nonce and honour `expires_at` on the ain path as part of 344's fix, and document both in the protocol section (288).
items.fixed_note: The nonce is checked against `expires_at` on both schemes and is spent last, after amount, signature and balance; on the AIN path the transfer must carry `transferKeyFor(resource, nonce)` and a payer signature over `x402-ain:<tx>:<nonce>`, so a quote is neither eternal nor a bearer ticket.

items.title: The receipt shows a transaction hash you cannot click
items.problem: The timeline prints `shortHash(r.tx_hash, 18)` as plain text (PatchPage.tsx:548) and the Ledger page's only external link points at the app subtree (`${provider}/get_value?ref=${app}`, LedgerPage.tsx:169), never at a transaction lookup — although the chain answers `ain_getTransactionByHash` for a purchase (verified for 0x353a6a…: FINALIZED, is_executed).
items.evidence: PatchPage.tsx:548-556; LedgerPage.tsx:169.
items.user_cost: The product says a payment is 'final once executed' and gives the buyer no one-click way to confirm that their payment executed.
items.fix: Link the hash in the receipt, the settle rows and the payouts table to the provider's transaction lookup.
items.fixed_note: On an AIN ledger the receipt's transaction hash, the line for a purchase already made, and every settle row in the History tab link to {provider}/get_transaction?hash=… — verified against the local chain, which answers FINALIZED / is_executed true for a real settlement. On a local ledger there is nothing to look up and no link is offered. RESIDUE in other groups' files: the payouts table on /account and the rows on /ledger.

items.title: 'verification confirmed' on the receipt implies a guarantee the terms explicitly disclaim
items.problem: The timeline renders a green 'verification confirmed' step (packages/web/src/i18n/pages/detail.ts:225) at the moment of payment, while /terms 2.3 says verification is best-effort, no deposit is escrowed and 'Verified does not guarantee that knowledge is always correct or free of side effects' (public.ts:181).
items.evidence: detail.ts:225 + PatchPage.tsx:556-561; public.ts:181; README.md:131.
items.user_cost: The buyer over-trusts a two-signature quorum as an audit, and meets the caveat only if they open the terms page.
items.fix: Label the step 'passed 2 of 2 independent checks (best-effort, not a guarantee)' and link the caveat inline; once 329 lands, name the executor count there too.
items.fixed_note: The timeline step reads "passed 2 of 2 independent checks" (KO 독립 검증 2/2 통과 확인) instead of "verification confirmed", and the receipt carries the caveat inline — best-effort, no deposit at stake, no promise the knowledge is correct or free of side effects — naming the distinct model servers behind those runs (item 329) and linking to the terms.

items.title: The advertised on-chain access receipt is best-effort and its failure is swallowed
items.surface: buy step 'access receipt recorded on the ledger'
items.problem: `recordAccess` is wrapped in a `.catch` that logs a warn and returns null, and the step is pushed only when a tx comes back (market.ts:815-817); `recordAccess` also returns null when the anchor has no `entry_id` (ain-ledger.ts:466-467). The step simply disappears from the timeline.
items.evidence: Code at HEAD; on the demo the receipts do write ('on-chain access receipt written'), so this is a silent-failure path rather than an observed loss.
items.user_cost: A buyer relying on the receipt as proof of purchase may have none and is never told.
items.fix: Show the failure as a warning step ('access receipt could not be written — retry'), retry it in the background, and stop describing it as guaranteed until it is.

items.title: Dev-chain AIN is labelled next to prices and nowhere else: the wallet total, the landing counts and the terms present it as money
items.problem: `price.ain_note` ('AIN = AI Network token (this demo runs a local dev chain)') is rendered under prices and the Buy button (PatchPage.tsx:229, :502, :531 — the earlier claim that the Buy tab omits it is wrong). What carries no label is the Account wallet total (AccountPage.tsx:133, note only in a `title=`), the landing figures, and terms 2.4, which distinguishes only AIN from node credit and never says a dev or test chain's AIN has no market value — the production plan proposes exactly that label (docs/production-verification-plan.md:347).
items.evidence: critic-buytab-nodeb-en-1280.png (the note IS on the buy tab); AccountPage.tsx:133; public.ts:183.
items.user_cost: The largest number a node operator sees — their balance — is the one with no provenance label, on a chain whose tokens are worth nothing.
items.fix: Derive `network_kind` (local / testnet / mainnet) from the provider and apply one consistent label to every AIN figure, including the wallet total and the terms.
items.fixed_note: One rule (utils/useNetwork) labels every AIN figure with the chain this node settles on, wallet total included, and terms 2.4 says a dev or test chain's AIN has no market value.

flows.name: F. Subscriptions and tracks
flows.description: The only recurring-revenue object in the product, and what it costs the two sides.

items.title: Subscribing spends the balance item by item, publishes the subscription before buying anything, and reports success when every purchase failed
items.problem: `subscribe` appends and broadcasts the public `subscribe` record first (market.ts:1097-1100), then loops `buy()` per item, logging each failure as a warn and continuing (market.ts:1105-1112); the function returns void, so the API answers `{ok:true}` and the CLI prints '✓ subscribed … (patches acquired and applied when a runtime is available)' with exit 0. `route()` then advertises the node as serving that track. (Item 260 covers the swallowed failure and the false closing text; the ledger-record-first ordering, the spend without a quote and the routing consequence are what remain.)
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/chain-buy-human-16-node-e-insufficient.txt (2 CREDIT: the cheapest item bought, 'insufficient credit: 0 < 3' for the rest, ✓ exit 0, wallet 0); chain-buy-agent-12-subscribe-peer-offline.txt (seller offline: ✓, purchases 0); chain-buy-human-28 (✓ with 0 CREDIT and the seller down).
items.user_cost: The buyer's last credits are spent on the first cheap item, they are told everything is fine, and the network routes requests to a node holding a third of the track — with no receipt and no way to know without reading the node log.
items.fix: Two-phase: `POST /api/branches/:name/quote` → `{items:[{id, price, seller, held, sellable}], total, balance}`, printed by the CLI and shown in a sheet before anything is spent; buy all items (ancestors first) and append the `subscribe` record only when every item is held, otherwise answer 409 `{acquired, failed:[{id,error}]}` and exit non-zero; record a partial subscription explicitly.
items.fixed_note: the node half: POST /api/branches/:name/quote prices every item before anything is spent, subscribe() buys everything BEFORE it appends and broadcasts the subscription record, a partial acquisition is 409 {acquired, failed[]} with nothing announced (verified live: the buyer keeps the three items it could afford, `mine: []`, and the gateway does not route to it), and the CLI asks [y/N] and exits non-zero. The web half shipped in 0d82cfb. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — `branch subscribe` prints the per-item plan and the total, asks before spending, refuses a non-terminal without --yes, and reports what was actually bought.

verified.by: adversarial re-test against a live node (port base 3790, NGRAM_RUNTIME_API=http://127.0.0.1:9)
verified.note: Web half re-tested 2026-09-04 (see finding 9): nothing is spent or broadcast before the confirm, the sheet states that the subscription record is written and broadcast BEFORE anything is bought, that failures are swallowed per item, and that unsubscribing refunds nothing. The two-phase quote, the ordering and the non-zero exit are node/CLI and still open.

items.title: Any node can take over a track by re-creating it under the same name: subscribers follow the new owner and the original owner is locked out
items.problem: `createBranch` never checks for an existing name (market.ts:949-957) and `branches()` is last-write-wins with an owner-only rule that exists on the AIN ledger alone (`local-ledger.ts:173` stores records by kind with no per-kind rule). So on a local-ledger network a second `create` of the same name rewrites the owner, the description and the item list for everyone; the real owner's `branch add` then fails with 403.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/subscriptions-21 (the owner column flips to the impostor; the original owner's `branch add` → 403); market.ts:949-964; local-ledger.ts:173. (Item 269 mentions last-write-wins only for undeletable test tracks.)
items.user_cost: A curated channel — the thing a subscriber pays for over time — can be taken over by anyone who knows its name, and the subscribers' nodes follow it.
items.fix: Refuse `createBranch` when the name exists and the caller is not the owner (400 `branch_exists`), enforce the owner rule in the local ledger as the chain rule does, and show the owner address on the track card so a takeover is visible.
items.fixed_note: the node that first wrote a track name owns it: Market.branches() drops a `branch` record for that name from anyone else (and the local ledger applies the same rule the AIN write rule does), createBranch refuses with 409 branch_exists naming the owner — reproduced live — and the console track card shows the owner. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — node-b creating node-a’s track name is refused with branch_exists naming the owner.

items.title: There is no subscription: every day of a daily track is a fresh full-price sale, and the curator earns nothing for curating
items.problem: `BranchInfo` carries name, description, context and patch ids and no terms (packages/core/src/types.ts:185-193); `Settlement` has no track field (market.ts:615-618); prices are per anchor and immutable (278), so a loyal subscriber pays the full price of every bake forever and a track owner who curates other people's knowledge (`addToBranch` accepts any existing entry, market.ts:975-984) receives nothing — there is no curator line in `royaltySplit`.
items.evidence: types.ts:185-193; market.ts:615-618, :975-984; catalog.ts:236-306. Confirmed against the daily-bake behaviour recorded in items 255-257.
items.user_cost: The one recurring-revenue shape the product describes has no price object, so the most loyal customer is the most expensive one and nobody is paid to keep a channel good.
items.fix: Give a branch optional terms (`price_per_period`, `included_items`, `curator_share`) signed by its owner; charge a subscription once per period instead of per item; carry `branch` on the settlement and add the curator to `royaltySplit`; show the run-rate ('about 12 CREDIT a month at one bake a day') on the track card before subscribing.

items.title: 'Pay per hour loaded' and 'pay per use' are offered to sellers and printed to buyers, and nothing is ever metered
items.surface: Publish form billing select; Buy tab billing label; `settlePayment`
items.problem: The `BillingModel` enum is accepted at publish (api.ts:301) and rendered by `f.billingLabel` ('pay per hour loaded', 'pay per use', packages/web/src/i18n/pages/detail.ts:49-50), but `settlePayment` charges `anchor.price` exactly once per 402 round and only copies `billing` onto the settlement (market.ts:576-627); grep for per_hit / per_apply_hour outside the enum and the labels finds nothing.
items.evidence: api.ts:301; detail.ts:49-50; market.ts:576-627. Not reported in any earlier review.
items.user_cost: A seller picks a revenue model the product does not implement, and a buyer is told they are paying by the hour when they paid once — the two models that would make serving other people's knowledge profitable exist only as words.
items.fix: Either implement metering (a `usage` record per applied hour or per answered request, settled in batches against the buyer's balance) or remove both options from the form and the labels until it exists.
items.fixed_note: PARTIAL — the /new-patch billing select is gone and the sale is described as one payment per download. The identical select on the draft-edit form (ManagePage.tsx:360-365) and detail.ts’s f.billingLabel for anchors already carrying those models are other groups’ files and still offer/print them.

items.title: The seller sees subscribers as a shrinking integer and track revenue as an undifferentiated sales list
items.problem: `subscribers` is derived from live subscribe/unsubscribe state (api.ts:251-254), so a node that unsubscribes simply vanishes — no churn, no history. Sales rows are `{patch_id, buyer, amount, at}` (api.ts:344) with no track attribution, so a seller cannot see what a track earns per bake, who left, or that the same buyer paid twice (271).
items.evidence: api.ts:251-254, :344; market.ts:615-618 (Settlement has no branch field). Seller-side track economics are not covered by items 194/195.
items.user_cost: The person deciding whether to keep baking every morning cannot see the only numbers that answer it.
items.fix: Keep the subscription history (an append-only view of subscribe/unsubscribe with timestamps), carry `branch` on settlements written for a subscription purchase, and show per-track revenue, subscriber count and churn on the track card and in `ainize wallet`.
items.fixed_note: Track pages read the subscribe records for joins, leaves and who left when, count what the track has sold per version, and the console's track card carries churn and the owner's earnings.

items.title: Purchases made by a subscription are indistinguishable from deliberate ones, and the Paid cell prints the unit twice
items.problem: `putPurchase` records no origin (market.ts:812) so a subscription's purchases look like manual ones; `DashboardPage.tsx:208` renders `money.fmt(amount, cur)` followed by `schemeText(scheme)`, which on a local-ledger node resolves to 'node credit' twice — '8 node credit (node credit)'.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/subscriptions-10 (dashboard text); DashboardPage.tsx:208; market.ts:812.
items.user_cost: The operator cannot tell what a track spent from what they chose to buy, and the money column reads like a bug.
items.fix: Store `origin: 'manual' | 'subscription:<track>'` on the purchase row, group the table by it with a per-track subtotal, and print the unit once.

flows.name: G. Incentives and the network view
flows.description: Why a peer shares rather than hoards or copies, where the money comes from, and what the network shows about itself.

items.title: A byte-identical copy of someone else's knowledge lists as a new root at a quarter of the price — and automatically retires the original
items.surface: `ainize publish` of a bought body; `reconcileSupersedes`; every catalogue
items.problem: `createDraft` checks the id, the model and the price and never compares `patch_sha256` with existing anchors (market.ts:330-345); nothing requires a publisher to hold a licence, declare a parent, or prove authorship of the bytes. Verifiers then PASS the copy — on a hash-only path the check is literally 'integrity=sha256 ok' — and `reconcileSupersedes` (market.ts:481) marks the newer, identical-row anchor as superseding the older one, network-wide. The original author's only sight of it is an 'overlaps' row three tabs deep and a warn line telling them their own knowledge has been retired.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/critique4-02-resold-copy-supersedes-the-original.txt: node-c buys ux4-paid for 8 CREDIT, republishes the same sha256 as ux4-resold at 2 CREDIT with no parents; node-a's own verifier attests it from its own blob store; node-a logs 'ux4-resold supersedes your knowledge ux4-paid — buyers now see "Newer version available" on it'; a neutral peer's `patch ls` shows ux4-paid SUPERSEDED and ux4-resold LISTED; `/api/patches/ux4-paid` → superseded_by ['ux4-resold'].
items.user_cost: The sharing economy's worst case, in three commands: a buyer resells the creator's file at any price, pays them nothing, and the product itself points every buyer from the original to the copy. There is no notice, no dispute, no takedown and no way to re-price in response (278).
items.fix: At draft time, refuse (409 `duplicate_body`) when `patch_sha256` matches a non-DRAFT anchor by another author unless the draft declares that anchor as a parent and the licence allows it — the address-set overlap the node already computes makes near-identical bodies detectable too. Never let an anchor supersede another author's anchor: restrict `reconcileSupersedes` to same-author pairs (or require the older author's signed consent, as item 150's fix proposes). Emit a `derived`/`copy` event to the original author with the copy's id, price and sha, and show 'identical body to <id> by <author>' on both knowledge pages.
items.fixed_note: Two halves, both closed. Draft time: createDraft refuses `duplicate_body` outright — with no --force override — when the exact bytes are already on the record under another author, and points at building on that knowledge instead. Record time: a supersede can only name an older anchor by the same author, so a copy can no longer retire the original (verified live with an overlapping rival publish from a second node). The original author is told: the node logs a warn event naming the copy, its author, its price and the shared sha the moment such an anchor arrives from a peer (verified live — a node that published the same bytes before it knew of the original was peered in, and the author's log carried the notice), and the manage page's overlap table now says who published each overlap and marks a byte-identical republish as one. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — publishing another node’s exact bytes is refused with duplicate_body, and --force does not override it.

items.title: On a local ledger every new keypair is worth 100 CREDIT: a seller's revenue is minted by whoever buys, and 'insufficient credit' is one key-rotation away
items.problem: `creditBalance` starts every address at `cfg.market.initialCredit` (default '100') and subtracts settled purchases (market.ts:670-680) — there is no faucet, no registration, no cap and no record of where the credit came from, so an address nobody has ever seen is solvent by definition. Local credit is the default ledger for `ainize init`, for the teach nodes and for every new operator.
items.evidence: critique4-01 helper (mint.mjs): a keypair created 200 ms earlier and funded by nothing signed an intent and bought an 8-CREDIT knowledge — `x-payment-response {"settled":true, "royalty":{"0x7025…":"8"}}`, a manifest, and the body; the seller's wallet now reads 'sales 2' and a balance of 108. teach-triggered-23 shows the same with a fresh browser key buying a lesson.
items.user_cost: Every number in the local economy — a seller's balance, a teacher's 'Paid', an ancestor's royalties — is denominated in money the buyer minted, and any spend limit can be bypassed by generating a key. It also makes the play-money disclosure (299) the only thing standing between a teacher and a false belief that they earned something.
items.fix: Make the grant explicit and finite: record it as a `grant` ledger record written once per address by the node that grants it (so `creditBalance` sums real records), cap it per node, and show 'starting credit granted by node-a' in the wallet; refuse to grant to an address with no history on a node that sells for AIN. Say on every local-credit surface that the credit is issued by this node and is not money.
items.fixed_note: Local credit is issued, not assumed: creditBalance sums a recorded `credit_grants` row plus royalties minus purchases, one grant per address written only after the buyer's signature proves the key exists, capped at market.creditGrants (default 100 addresses), never on a node that sells for AIN, and the node grants itself the same way at startup. GET /api/credit/:address says where the credit came from, how many grants are gone and that it is not money; the CLI quote and the Buy tab print that sentence where the money is about to be spent. Addresses are compared case-insensitively there too. Verified live: a fresh keypair's balance came from a recorded grant with a reason, and the issuance count moved 1 → 3. ADVERSARIAL RE-CHECK: reproduced live — GET /api/credit/<never-seen address> answers balance 0 with would_grant, and a grant is recorded, capped and attributed once the address first signs a payment.

items.title: A seller can buy its own knowledge: sold count, revenue and the 'Most popular' ranking all inflate, and the purchases look like anyone else's
items.problem: `settlePayment` checks that the seller is the anchor's author but never that the buyer is not (market.ts:686, :704-712), and `buy()` has no self check (`subscribe` skips own anchors, market.ts:1109, but nothing else does). `deriveCatalog` counts every settlement as a download (catalog.ts:141) and `sort: 'popular'` orders by that count (api.ts:168) — the ranking the landing page's Trending row uses.
items.evidence: packages/e2e/results/ux4/incentives-network-ns-11 (three self-buys → SOLD 5 on every peer, revenue up, ranking up); catalog.ts:141; api.ts:168. Free items make it costless (277).
items.user_cost: The only demand signal on the marketplace can be manufactured for nothing, and a buyer comparing two knowledges is reading it.
items.fix: Refuse a settlement whose buyer is the seller (400 `self_purchase`), exclude self-settlements from `downloads`, `revenue` and the popular sort when historic ones exist, and count distinct buyers rather than settlements in the ranking.

items.title: At the default price a sale on a real chain costs more gas than it earns, and nothing warns the publisher
items.problem: `defaultPrice` is '0.1' (packages/core/src/config.ts:210) and every royalty line is a separate transfer (`payouts.ts:66-75`, one row per (settle, address), each sent with its own `wallet.transfer`, :93). The product's own estimate is ~0.19 AIN of gas around a 0.1 AIN purchase at `min_gas_price 500` (docs/production-verification-plan.md:264), and the dev chain hides it by sending `gas_price 0` (ain-ledger.ts:233). The publish form gives no pricing guidance at all (item 162) and no gas note.
items.evidence: config.ts:210; payouts.ts:66-93; production-verification-plan.md:264; ain-ledger.ts:233.
items.user_cost: The default price makes every sale a loss on the network the product is heading to, and a family of three ancestors multiplies the loss by the number of payout transfers.
items.fix: Compute a price floor from the provider's `min_gas_price` and the number of payees, warn on the publish form and in `ainize publish` when the price is below it, and batch a settlement's payouts into one transaction (or net them against the seller's next purchase) so one sale costs one write.

items.title: A seller cannot see who holds their file: the holder set exists in the manifest and on no screen
items.problem: `issueManifest` lists every holder as a download URL (market.ts:747) and `/api/nodes` reports a `blobs` count per peer, but no seller-facing surface answers 'who has my file and why' — `patch get` shows sold/revenue/settlements, the Manage page shows attestations and overlaps, and neither distinguishes a paying buyer from a verifier's free copy (327) or a peer that mirrored it.
items.evidence: market.ts:747; packages/cli/src/commands/patch.ts:47-110; verifier-economy-demo-network-en-1280.png (BLOBS column with no per-knowledge view).
items.user_cost: Replication is the product's answer to a dead seller (276) and its biggest leak (326-327) at the same time, and the seller can see neither side of it.
items.fix: Show 'held by N nodes: 2 buyers, 3 verifiers, 1 mirror' on the Manage page and in `patch get`, from `p2p.holders` joined with settlements and roles.
items.fixed_note: The manage page lists every node holding the file with the reason the record gives — publisher, buyer, verifier or mirror — under one line counting the four.

items.title: A node's terms — creator share, contributor share, quorum, ledger, price policy — are invisible and incomparable, although every node publishes them
items.problem: `/api/info` exposes `royalty_share` and quorum (api.ts:137-142) and the knowledge page prints the VIEWING node's rate as if it were the network's (PatchPage.tsx:437-447 — the seller's own rate is item 191). The Network table shows none of it, so a creator choosing where to publish or teach, and a buyer wondering what share their money will split, have nothing to compare.
items.evidence: api.ts:137-142; NetworkPage.tsx:106-128; PatchPage.tsx:437-447.
items.user_cost: In a market of peers with different terms, the terms are the product — and they are the one column missing from the only page that lists the peers.
items.fix: Add creator share, contributor share, quorum, ledger and default price to `/api/nodes` and the Network table, and label the knowledge page's share sentence with whose rate it is (the anchor's, once 191's fix writes it there).
items.fixed_note: PeerInfo carries quorum, default price and accepts_contributions beside `shares`, filled by selfInfo, and /network shows each peer's terms; a node running an older build reads "not published".

items.title: Node credit is a derived number whose starting grant is each seller's own setting: the same buyer is solvent at one seller and refused at another
items.surface: `creditBalance`; Buy tab 'Pays from this node's credit balance'
items.problem: `creditBalance` derives a balance from settle records, which are gossiped, so within one local-ledger network every node computes the same figure for an address — but the starting grant is `this.cfg.market.initialCredit` (market.ts:671), so a seller configured with 10 sees a different balance than one configured with 100, and a buyer with an identical history can be refused by one and served by the other. The Buy tab says only 'Pays from this node's credit balance'; only /terms 2.4 says it is development money.
items.evidence: market.ts:670-680; config.ts:212; packages/web/src/i18n/pages/detail.ts (`detail.buy.pays_from_credit`).
items.user_cost: 'Insufficient credit' can mean 'you spent it' or 'this seller grants less than the last one', and nothing on the surface distinguishes them.
items.fix: Make the grant a record (364) so it is the same on every node, name the granting node in the balance line, and print in the refusal which grant and which spends produced the figure.

praise.headline: The settle record is the right primitive, and the split inside it is correct.
praise.detail: Every sale writes one public record carrying the full per-address royalty map; `royaltySplit` walks the ancestor graph with a visited set and a depth cut, clamps every share into [0,1], carves each contributor from a fixed remainder (the §11 pass-2 fix is in the tree) and can never distribute more than the price — every split produced in this round, across children, merges, undercuts and data providers, summed to the price to the cent. The gateway even hands the buyer the whole map in `x-payment-response` at settle time. Almost every money fix in this review is display and delivery over numbers the product already computes correctly.

praise.headline: Payout rows are written the way money code should be written.
praise.detail: `payouts.enqueue` writes a durable row before any transfer is attempted, each attempt claims it atomically, and a row found mid-transfer after a restart is marked failed with the exact sentence an operator needs and is never auto-retried (payouts.ts:64-105, :152-162). Driven with a fake wallet it behaved exactly as documented. It needs to become visible and reconcilable — not rewritten.

praise.headline: The purchase path and `patch get` tell the truth.
praise.detail: `ainize patch buy` prints a millisecond timeline (quorum → quote → pay → settled → download → receipt), verifies the body against the on-ledger sha256 whichever peer served it, and names the file and the next command; `ainize patch get` is the one surface that shows a family honestly — each parent with its status, the superseded-by line, the address-set overlap table and the settlements — while the web tree still hides status in a tooltip. The CLI is the model the web should copy.

praise.headline: The teacher's earnings page is the honest version of the creator wallet.
praise.detail: `teacherProfile` reconciles what the public record says is owed against what this node's payout rows say was paid, names the seller per line, and says out loud what it cannot know: "recorded by {seller} — this node cannot see that transfer". A visitor with only a browser key can audit what they are owed without trusting the node. Item 311's fix is to point the wallet at this code.

praise.headline: The challenge loop works end to end with nobody in charge — and refuses fast when it would waste GPU.
praise.detail: A challenge took an item off sale within a second (423, with the challenger and the reason in the body — the best error text in the product), other verifiers re-ran the benchmark on their own, and the item re-listed 75 seconds later with no operator action. The verifier refuses before spending model time when its result could not count — a self-attestation, or a re-run whose record the derivation would discard — and says which rule applies and what would change it.

praise.headline: Uncomfortable truths are stated rather than decorated.
praise.detail: The deposit that was never escrowed was removed from every surface instead of being half-implemented, and the terms, the glossary, the README and the verifier all now say the same true thing. Prices carry "node credit = development play money" and "AIN = AI Network token (this demo runs a local dev chain)". The keep-private sheet names the hardware you would need to run your lesson yourself and admits there is no laptop version. And L0/L1 put `derivation`, `base.stack`, `dataset` access and a closed licence list on the anchor — the data model most of this review's fixes need already exists on the record.

order_of_work.wave: Wave N — close the paywall (two weeks; mostly one table and four call sites).
order_of_work.detail: Items 326, 327, 345, 344, 343, 336, 363, 365, 302. A `licenses` table (patch_id, source: purchase | author | verification) written by `putPurchase`, `announce` and the verifier; `applyPatch`, `testablePatches`, `chat` and `subscribe` ask it instead of `blobs.has`; verifier fetches become a lease that ends at the attestation and the body is dropped; `/p2p/hello` is signed; the download token is bound to the buyer; the AIN settlement is bound to the nonce, the resource and the payer; a duplicate `patch_sha256` by another author is refused and `reconcileSupersedes` never crosses authors. Nothing else in this review matters while the file is free to everyone who could resell it.

order_of_work.wave: Wave O — make paying idempotent and recoverable (one week, all S/M).
order_of_work.detail: Items 271, 272, 273, 274, 350, 352, 279, 346, 289, 293, 294. Look up the settlement before paying; consume the nonce last; re-issue the manifest to the recorded buyer; write the payment intent before the money moves; distinguish the four 'already used' cases; name the seller in a rejection; record the seller on the purchase row. This is the wave that stops the product from taking money twice and losing files once.

order_of_work.wave: Wave P — pay the people the record already names (two weeks, M).
order_of_work.detail: Items 309, 310, 313, 314, 311, 316, 315, 317, 321, 320, 319, 323, 324, 322.
